definition_zh: 火山；火山口；潜伏的危机
definition_en: a mountain with a vent in the earth, from which lava, ash and hot gas can burst out
core_image: 山顶裂开一道口子，滚烫的岩浆顺着山坡淌下来
scene: 岛上的居民半夜被闷响惊醒，窗外山顶正冒出暗红色的光。Through the night, the volcano poured glowing lava down its northern slope.
sceneCN: 这里 volcano 是「火山」（第 1 个义项：能够喷出熔岩与火山灰的山体）；句意为整夜里火山把发光的熔岩顺着北坡倾泻下来。山顶裂开冒红光的那幅画就是这个词给人的印象。

pos.zh: 火山；火山口；潜伏的危机

collocations.zh: 怒气的火山：一触即发的情绪

derivatives.zh: 由 volcano 加 -ic 构成，义为「火山的；火山般的」
加 -ally 构成，义为「火山似地；剧烈地」
加 -ism 构成，义为「火山作用；火山现象」
加 -logy 构成，义为「火山学」
加 -logist 构成，义为「火山学家」

senses.title: A mountain that can erupt
senses.definition: a mountain or hill with an opening in the earth through which lava, ash and gas escape
senses.definitionCN: 地表有出口、能喷出熔岩、火山灰与气体的山体
senses.example: Through the night, the volcano poured glowing lava down its northern slope.
senses.exampleCN: 整夜里，火山把发光的熔岩顺着北坡倾泻下来。
senses.why: The Italian island of Vulcano was thought to be the workshop of the fire god, and the whole kind of mountain took its name.
senses.whyCN: 意大利小岛武尔卡诺被认为火神的工作场，这一类山便借用了它的名字。

senses.title: The vent of a volcano
senses.definition: the vent or opening itself, rather than the whole cone around it
senses.definitionCN: 火山喷出口本身，而非周边整座锥体
senses.example: Sensors were lowered into the volcano to measure the rising heat.
senses.exampleCN: 为测量上升的热量，探测器被放进火山口里。
senses.why: The name points first at the hole through which fire comes up; the mountain around it was named afterwards.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最先指的是火冒出来的那个口子，周围的山体后来才被一并命名。

senses.title: The god of fire in old belief
senses.definition: in older use, the workshop of the fire god or the fire believed to burn beneath the ground
senses.definitionCN: 早期用法里指火神的作坊，或被认为在地下燃烧的火
senses.example: Old sailors told of a volcano beneath the sea where the fire god worked.
senses.exampleCN: 老水手讲起海面之下有座火山，火神就在那里干活。
senses.why: Before geology, fire from the ground was explained by a god; Vulcan ruled that fire and his name stayed in the mountain.
senses.whyCN: 在地质学出现以前，地下冒出的火用神来解释；火神伏尔甘掌管这火，他的名字留在了山上。

senses.title: The volcanic adjective
senses.definition: relating to, or produced by, a volcano, as in volcanic rock and volcanic ash
senses.definitionCN: 与火山有关的、由火山产生的，如火山岩与火山灰
senses.example: The village sits on volcanic rock that keeps the soil rich.
senses.exampleCN: 村庄坐落在使土壤肥沃的火山岩上。
senses.why: Adding -ic turns the mountain into a describing word, so the adjective covers everything a volcano makes.
senses.whyCN: 加上 -ic，山就变成修饰词，于是这个词覆盖了火山产出的一切。

senses.title: A temper ready to blow
senses.titleCN: 火山般的情绪；一触即发
senses.definition: a state of feeling or a situation that is under pressure and may explode at any moment
senses.definitionCN: 受压、随时可能爆发的情绪或局面
senses.example: His anger was a volcano that no one dared to set off.
senses.exampleCN: 他的怒气像一座火山，没人敢去点燃。
senses.why: A volcano rests quietly for years and then bursts without warning; that is exactly how a held-in temper behaves.
senses.whyCN: 火山安静多年却毫无预警地爆发，忍耐着的脾气正是这副样子。

intro.en: Volcano is named after the small island of Vulcano, which was taken as the chimney of the fire god.
intro.cn: volcano 以小岛武尔卡诺命名，古代认为那里是火神的烟囱。

items.en: Vulcanus was the Roman god of fire and of metalwork, and his name is the seed of the word.
items.cn: Vulcanus 是罗马的火与锻造之神，这个名字就是本词的种子。

items.en: Vulcano, one of the Aeolian Islands, was seen as a workshop where smoke rose from the ground.
items.cn: 武尔卡诺是伊奥利亚群岛之一，人们把那里看作地面冒烟的作坊。

items.en: Deeper roots of Vulcanus are debated; some link it to a word for lightning, but no solution is settled.
items.cn: Vulcanus 更早的来源有争议，有人认为与表示闪电的词有关，但尚无定论。

items.en: In the sixteenth century Italian writers used vulcano for any fire-breathing mountain, and the range of meaning widened.
items.cn: 十六世纪意大利作家用 vulcano 指任何喷火的山，这个词的所指扩大。

items.en: English adopted the word in the seventeenth century and kept the plural volcanoes in common use.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪引入该词，复数 volcanoes 成为通用形式。

items.en: Geology then split the image into the cone, its vent, its products and the metaphor of exploding feeling.
items.cn: 此后地质学把这个形象分成山锥、喷口、产物以及「情绪爆发」的比喻。

note.en: The first group gathers words built on the name of the fire god, the second the other landforms and fire words near it.
note.cn: 第一组收以火神之名为基础的词，第二组收相近的地貌词与火相关词。

entries.definition: The usual plural form of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 复数，最常见的形式。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning of or made by a volcano.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「火山的、由火山造成的」。

entries.definition: The Roman fire god whose name the mountain carries.
entries.definitionCN: 罗马火神，这座山沿用了他的名字。

entries.definition: The noun for the whole set of volcanic processes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指火山活动的总体过程。

entries.definition: The bowl-shaped opening at the top of a volcano.
entries.definitionCN: 火山顶部的碗状开口。

entries.definition: The hot melted rock that a volcano pours out.
entries.definitionCN: 火山喷出的炽热熔岩。

entries.definition: The melted rock still below the ground, not yet erupted.
entries.definitionCN: 尚在地下、尚未喷出的岩浆。

entries.definition: Shaking of the ground, often in the same regions as volcanoes.
entries.definitionCN: 地震，常与火山出现在同一区域。

normalIntro.en: One named island, one fire god, and a set of ordinary English endings explain the whole family.
normalIntro.cn: 一座得名的小岛、一位火神，加上普通英语后缀，就能解释整个词族。

normal.en: Volcano, volcanic and volcanology all rest on the god Vulcan.
normal.cn: volcano、volcanic、volcanology 都建立在火神伏尔甘的名字上。

normal.en: The plural is volcanoes, with an e before the s.
normal.cn: 复数是 volcanoes，s 前要加 e。

normal.en: Lava is outside, magma is inside; both come from a volcano.
normal.cn: lava 在地上，magma 在地下，两者都出自火山。

normal.en: An active volcano erupts now, a dormant one sleeps.
normal.cn: active volcano 现在喷发，dormant volcano 正在沉睡。

normal.en: Used of people, the word keeps the image: a volcano of anger.
normal.cn: 用于人时意象仍在：volcano of anger（怒火如火山）。

abstract.en: See a dark cone at night with one red line running down its side.
abstract.cn: 想夜里一座黑色的锥形山，侧面拖着一条红线。

abstract.en: Hear a low rumble under the floor long before anything is seen.
abstract.cn: 想在地面之下先听到低沉的闷响，许久之后才见东西。

abstract.en: Feel a held-in temper waiting, quiet and hot, behind a shut door.
abstract.cn: 感受一扇关着的门后，压抑的脾气安静而灼热地等着。

examples.en: The volcano has been quiet for two hundred years.
examples.cn: 这座火山已经安静了两百年。

examples.en: Ash from the volcano covered the fields for weeks.
examples.cn: 火山灰覆盖田野达数周之久。

examples.en: Scientists mapped the inside of the volcano with sound waves.
examples.cn: 科学家用声波绘制了火山内部的结构。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「火山口的老肯」——老肯守在火山口边，看见红汤往外冒。

root: 拉丁语 Vulcanus（罗马火神）→ 意大利语 vulcano（火山，源自小岛武尔卡诺）→ 英语 volcano；更早词源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as a named island and a god, then covers the mountain, its opening, what it produces, and the metaphor of feelings about to burst.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从一座得名的小岛与一位神出发，先指山体，再指喷口、火山产物，最后比喻随时爆发的情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mountain with a red crack at the top.
core.cn: 核心意象：山顶有一道红色裂口的山。

branches.en: The mountain branch: a cone pouring lava down its slope.
branches.cn: 山体分支：熔岩顺坡流下的锥形山。

branches.en: The opening branch: the vent itself, measured and studied.
branches.cn: 开口分支：喷口本身，被测量与研究。

branches.en: The old belief branch: the fire god at work underground.
branches.cn: 旧信仰分支：火神在地下干活。

branches.en: The adjective branch: volcanic rock under a village.
branches.cn: 形容词分支：村庄下方的火山岩。

branches.en: The temper branch: anger that no one dares to set off.
branches.cn: 脾气分支：没人敢点燃的怒火。

intro.en: Volcan- is a name, not a Latin meaning; the endings -o, -ic, -ism and -ology do the building after the name was borrowed.
intro.cn: volcan- 是一个专名而非拉丁义素；后缀 -o、-ic、-ism、-ology 在名字借入后承担构词。

latinIntro.en: The name goes back to the Roman god Vulcanus; a Latin god name is recorded, so only the deeper root is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 名字上溯到罗马神名 Vulcanus；神名有文献记录，只有更早词根不确定。

items.example: The god gave his name to the island.
items.exampleCN: 这位神把自己的名字给了那座岛。
武尔卡诺岛位于西西里附近。

items.example: The Italian ending stayed on the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 意大利语词尾保留在英语名词上。

items.example: An active volcano is watched day and night.

definition_zh: 伏特；伏；电压单位；（旧）环骑步法
definition_en: a unit of electrical force, defined as the push that moves one ampere through one ohm
core_image: 一节干电池上标着一个数字，指针随之轻轻一摆
scene: 实验课上，老师把万用表接到旧电池两端，读数只剩一点点。The battery had lost half a volt, so the lamp would not light.
sceneCN: 这里 volt 是「伏特」（第 1 个义项：电压单位）；句意为这节电池少了半伏，灯就点不亮了。表盘上指针轻摆的那一刻就是这个单位在做的事。

pos.zh: 伏特（电压单位）；伏

derivatives.zh: 由 volt 加 -age 构成，义为「电压」
volt 与 meter（计量器）复合，义为「伏特计；电压表」
volt 与 ampere 复合，义为「伏安」，视在功率单位

senses.title: The unit of electric force
senses.definition: the unit used to measure the force that drives a current in a circuit
senses.definitionCN: 衡量电路中推动电流的力量大小的单位
senses.example: The battery had lost half a volt, so the lamp would not light.
senses.exampleCN: 这节电池少了半伏，灯就点不亮了。
senses.why: The unit is named after Alessandro Volta, who built the first steady source of current; his name became the measure of the push itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个单位以亚历山德罗·伏打命名，他造出第一个稳定的电流源，他的名字就成了「推力」本身的度量。

senses.title: A unit in compound names
senses.definition: used inside larger unit names such as electron volt and kilovolt
senses.definitionCN: 用于电子伏、千伏等更大单位名称之中
senses.example: A kilovolt is a thousand units of electric force.
senses.exampleCN: 一千伏就是电压的一千个单位。
senses.why: A practical unit is too small for power lines and too large for chips, so the word is attached to prefixes.
senses.whyCN: 实用单位对电力线路太小、对芯片又太大，于是这个词被挂上各种前缀。

senses.title: The measured value in speech
senses.definition: the number of volts actually present, as read from a meter
senses.definitionCN: 从表上读出的、实际存在的电压数值
senses.example: The reading dropped to three volts within a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 读数在一分钟内降到三伏。
senses.why: Once the unit exists, people stop saying the unit and just quote the number as a plain count of volts.
senses.whyCN: 单位一旦确立，人们就不再说单位本身，而直接把数值当作伏特的计数来讲。

senses.title: The name of the inventor
senses.definition: the surname of the Italian scientist whose experiments gave electricity a steady push
senses.definitionCN: 意大利科学家的姓氏，他的实验给了电流稳定的推动力
senses.example: Volta showed that two metals and a wet cloth could move a current.
senses.exampleCN: 伏打证明两种金属加一块湿布就能推动电流。
senses.why: Scientific units often borrow the name of the person who made the measurement possible; here the name kept its capital only for the man.
senses.whyCN: 科学单位常借用促成测量之人的名字，这里只有写人时才保留大写。

senses.title: Round in a riding manoeuvre
senses.definition: in older fencing and riding language, a turn or a circular step to one side
senses.definitionCN: 旧时击剑与马术用语里，向一侧的转身或绕行步
senses.example: The rider performed a volt before the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 骑手在门前走了一个环步。
senses.why: This is a separate Italian borrowing from voltare, to turn; only the spelling matches the electrical unit.
senses.whyCN: 这是另从意大利语 voltare（转）借来的词，只是拼写与电压单位相同，来源不同。

intro.en: Volt is a scientist surname turned into a unit; the older riding word is a separate Italian borrowing that happens to look the same.
intro.cn: volt 由科学家姓氏变为单位；较早的马术语则是另一个意大利语借词，只是拼写相同。

items.en: The surname Volta belongs to an Italian family from Como, and its origin is uncertain.
items.cn: Volta 是科莫一户意大利人家的姓氏，来源不确定。

items.en: Alessandro Volta built the pile that produced a steady current, which made exact measurement possible.
items.cn: 亚历山德罗·伏打造出能产生稳定电流的电堆，使精确测量成为可能。

items.en: In the eighteen sixties the international electrical congress adopted volt as the unit of force.
items.cn: 十九世纪六十年代，国际电学会议采用 volt 作为电压单位。

items.en: Prefixed forms such as millivolt and kilovolt spread with telegraphy and power supply.
items.cn: 毫伏、千伏等带前缀形式随电报与供电普及。

items.en: The separate riding term volt entered from French and Italian voltare, to turn, and remains rare.
items.cn: 另一个马术语 volt 来自法语与意大利语 voltare（转），如今很少使用。

note.en: The first group holds the family built on the unit, the second the other electrical measures it works with.
note.cn: 第一组收以该单位为基础的词族，第二组收与它配合的其他电学量度。

entries.definition: The plain plural of the unit.
entries.definitionCN: 该单位的普通复数。

entries.definition: The noun for the amount of electric force, measured in volts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电压」，以伏特计量。

entries.definition: An instrument that reads volts directly.
entries.definitionCN: 直接读出伏特数的仪器。

entries.definition: The surname of the Italian scientist behind the unit.
entries.definitionCN: 促成该单位的意大利科学家姓氏。

entries.definition: The unit of current, the flow that a volt drives.
entries.definitionCN: 电流单位，即伏特所推动的流动。

entries.definition: The unit of resistance, opposing that flow.
entries.definitionCN: 电阻单位，阻碍这种流动。

entries.definition: The unit of power, volts times amperes.
entries.definitionCN: 功率单位，等于伏特乘以安培。

entries.definition: The flow of charge itself, measured in amperes.
entries.definitionCN: 电荷流动本身，以安培计量。

normalIntro.en: One name, one unit, and three plain endings carry the whole family.
normalIntro.cn: 一个名字、一个单位，加上三个普通后缀，就撑起整个词族。

normal.en: Volt comes from the surname of Alessandro Volta; it is a name, not a Latin idea.
normal.cn: volt 来自亚历山德罗·伏打的姓氏，是专名而非拉丁义素。

normal.en: Volt measures the push, ampere the flow, ohm the resistance.
normal.cn: volt 量推力，ampere 量流动，ohm 量阻力。

normal.en: Voltage is the amount, volt is the unit; we say a voltage of five volts.
normal.cn: voltage 是量，volt 是单位；说 a voltage of five volts。

normal.en: A voltmeter reads volts; the -meter part means a measuring device.
normal.cn: voltmeter 读伏特，-meter 表示计量器。

normal.en: The plural is volts, with no change to the stem.
normal.cn: 复数是 volts，词干不变。

abstract.en: See a small battery with a printed number on its side.
abstract.cn: 想一节小电池，侧面印着一个数字。

abstract.en: Feel a gentle push travelling through a wire, like water under pressure.
abstract.cn: 感受一股轻推沿导线前行，像有压力的水。

abstract.en: Hear a needle swing and settle on a marked line.
abstract.cn: 听指针摆一下，停在刻度线上。

examples.en: The old radio works on nine volts.
examples.cn: 这台旧收音机用九伏电压工作。

examples.en: A single volt is a very small push for a machine.
examples.cn: 对一台机器来说，一伏是很小的推力。

examples.en: He measured the volt drop across the wire.
examples.cn: 他测了导线两端的电压降。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「沃特」——沃特拿着电池说：电压得按伏特来算。

root: 意大利语姓氏 Volta（亚历山德罗·伏打）→ 英语单位名 volt；姓氏本身的来源不确定。另有马术语 volt 来自意大利语 voltare（转），与电压单位无关。

sensesIntro.en: A surname becomes a unit, then a compound part, then a number people quote, then the man again, and finally a look-alike riding word from another root.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个姓氏变作单位，再做复合单位的一部分、成为人们直接报出的数字、回到那位科学家，最后是与它同形的另一个来源的马术语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one battery and one swinging needle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一节电池与一根摆动的指针。

branches.en: The unit branch: one volt of push through a circuit.
branches.cn: 单位分支：推动电路的一伏。

branches.en: The compound branch: millivolt, kilovolt, electron volt.
branches.cn: 复合分支：毫伏、千伏、电子伏。

branches.en: The reading branch: the meter shows three volts.
branches.cn: 读数分支：表上显示三伏。

branches.en: The person branch: Volta and his pile.
branches.cn: 人物分支：伏打与他的电堆。

branches.en: The riding branch: a turn before the gate.
branches.cn: 马术分支：门前的一次绕行。

intro.en: Volt-, Volta- carry only a name; -age, -meter and -s build the rest.
intro.cn: volt-、volta- 只携带专名信息，-age、-meter、-s 承担其余构词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root meaning electricity here; the family rests on an Italian surname of uncertain origin.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有表示电的拉丁词根，整个词族建立在来源不确定的意大利姓氏上。

items.meaning: the inventor of the electric pile
items.example: Volta taught physics in Como and Pavia.
items.exampleCN: 伏打在科莫与帕维亚教物理学。

items.example: The unit was fixed in his honour.
Volts divided by ohms give amperes.

definition_zh: 电压；电压值；电位差
definition_en: the measured amount of electric force between two points in a circuit
core_image: 两根导线之间的落差，像水从高处落向低处
scene: 维修工把表笔分别搭在插座的两个孔上，屏幕立刻跳出一个数字。He checked the voltage before touching any wire in the old house.
sceneCN: 这里 voltage 是「电压」（第 1 个义项：两点之间的电势差）；句意为他在碰这栋老房子里任何电线之前先量了电压。表笔一搭、数字跳出，正是这个词所指的量。

pos.zh: 电压；电压值；电位差

derivatives.zh: 去掉后缀 -age 得到的单位名，义为「伏特」
加 -ic 构成，义为「伏打电流的」
复合形容词，义为「高压的；精力充沛的」

senses.title: The force between two points
senses.definition: the difference in electric potential between two points, which drives a current
senses.definitionCN: 两点之间的电势差，正是它推动电流
senses.example: He checked the voltage before touching any wire in the old house.
senses.exampleCN: 在碰这栋老房子的任何电线之前，他先量了电压。
senses.why: Volt is the unit; -age makes a noun of amount, so voltage is literally how many volts lie between two points.
senses.whyCN: volt 是单位，-age 把量变成名词，所以 voltage 字面上就是两点之间有多少伏。

senses.title: The value on a meter
senses.definition: the figure a meter shows for that force, as a measured value
senses.definitionCN: 仪表显示出的这个力的数值，作为测量结果
senses.example: The voltage on the screen rose slowly as the sun hit the panel.
senses.exampleCN: 阳光照到面板上时，屏幕上的电压缓缓上升。
senses.why: Once a quantity can be read off a dial, the word refers to the figure itself rather than to the invisible push.
senses.whyCN: 量一旦能从表盘读出，这个词就指那个数字，而不是看不见的推力。

senses.title: A supply rated for a voltage
senses.definition: the level of electric force a device or a supply is built to use
senses.definitionCN: 电器或电源被设计使用的电力水平
senses.example: The lamp needs the right voltage or it will burn out.
senses.exampleCN: 这盏灯需要合适的电压，否则会烧坏。
senses.why: Manufacturers must state a level, so the word also names the condition a device expects.
senses.whyCN: 制造商必须标出水平，于是这个词也指设备所期待的条件。

senses.title: A difference to be stepped up or down
senses.definition: the level that transformers raise or lower between a power line and a home
senses.definitionCN: 变压器在电力线路与家庭之间升高或降低的水平
senses.example: A transformer cut the voltage before the current entered the street.
senses.exampleCN: 变压器在电流进入街道之前降低了电压。
senses.why: Because it is a difference between points, it can be changed up or down without any charge being created.
senses.whyCN: 因为它只是两点之间的差，所以可以随意升降，并不产生新的电荷。

senses.title: Lively force in a figurative sense
senses.titleCN: （比喻）高压般的劲头；激烈程度
senses.definition: in informal use, high energy or tension in a situation or a performance
senses.definitionCN: 口语中形容场面或表演里的高能量与紧张感
senses.example: The band played with real voltage from the first bar.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队从第一小节起就带着十足的劲头。
senses.why: A high voltage is dangerous and hard to ignore, so the word has been borrowed for anything thrilling or tense.
senses.whyCN: 高电压危险又难以忽视，于是这个词被借来形容任何刺激或紧张的东西。

intro.en: Voltage is a plain English build on the unit volt: the unit plus the noun ending -age.
intro.cn: voltage 是在单位 volt 上做的普通英语构造：单位加名词后缀 -age。

items.en: The unit rests on the surname of Alessandro Volta, whose pile first gave a steady current.
items.cn: 单位建立在亚历山德罗·伏打的姓氏上，他的电堆首次提供稳定电流。

items.en: The unit name volt was agreed by electrical congresses in the eighteen sixties.
items.cn: 单位名 volt 由十九世纪六十年代的电学会议确定。

items.en: The ending came to English through the Old French noun ending that meant a state or a quantity.
items.cn: 这个后缀经由表示状态或数量的古法语名词词尾进入英语。

items.en: Voltage is recorded from the late nineteenth century, when ordinary households began to have wiring.
items.cn: voltage 自十九世纪后期有记录，当时普通家庭开始装电线。

items.en: Twentieth-century electronics added compound uses such as low voltage and voltage drop.
items.cn: 二十世纪的电子学又添出 low voltage、voltage drop 这类复合用法。

note.en: The first group gathers the words built on the unit, the second the other electrical quantities measured beside it.
note.cn: 第一组收以该单位为基础的词，第二组收与它并列测量的其他电学量。

entries.definition: The plural form of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词复数。

entries.definition: The bare unit from which the noun is built.
entries.definitionCN: 构成该名词的裸单位。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning relating to current produced by chemical action.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「由化学作用产生电流的」。

entries.definition: The instrument used to read voltage.
entries.definitionCN: 用来读取电压的仪器。

entries.definition: The electric potential itself; the difference between two potentials is a voltage.
entries.definitionCN: 电势本身；两个电势之差就是电压。

entries.definition: The flow of charge, which a voltage drives.
entries.definitionCN: 电荷的流动，由电压推动。

entries.definition: The opposition to that flow.
entries.definitionCN: 对这种流动的阻力。

entries.definition: The rate of energy delivered, voltage times current.
entries.definitionCN: 能量输送的速率，等于电压乘电流。

normalIntro.en: One unit, one suffix, and the electrical neighbours next door.
normalIntro.cn: 一个单位、一个后缀，再加上隔壁那几位电学邻居。

normal.en: Voltage is volt plus -age: a number of volts said as one quantity.
normal.cn: voltage 是 volt 加 -age：把若干伏特当一个量来说。

normal.en: Say a voltage of five volts, not a voltage of five.
normal.cn: 要说 a voltage of five volts，而不是 a voltage of five。

normal.en: Voltage drives, current flows, resistance opposes.
normal.cn: 电压推，电流流，电阻阻。

normal.en: A voltage drop is the fall between two points along a wire.
normal.cn: voltage drop 是沿导线两点之间的下降。

normal.en: High-voltage can describe a lively person as well as a line.
normal.cn: high-voltage 既能形容线路，也能形容精力充沛的人。

abstract.en: Picture water in a high tank, waiting for a tap to open.
abstract.cn: 想高塔里的水，等着水龙头打开。

abstract.en: See two ends of a wire at different heights on a climbing wall.
abstract.cn: 想一根导线的两端挂在攀岩墙的不同高度。

abstract.en: Feel the click of a switch making that difference do work.
abstract.cn: 感受开关一合，那个差开始干活。

examples.en: The voltage in this socket is too high for the small toy.
examples.cn: 这个插座的电压对这件小玩具来说太高了。

examples.en: Engineers lowered the voltage to protect the lamps.
examples.cn: 工程师降低电压以保护灯泡。

examples.en: A steady voltage keeps the machine running smoothly.
examples.cn: 稳定的电压让机器运转顺畅。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「握太紧」——握住电线时手别太紧，先看清电压数字。

root: volt（伏特，来自意大利姓氏 Volta）+ 英语后缀 -age（量、状态）→ voltage；后缀经古法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: One quantity grows four ways: an invisible difference between points, a figure on a dial, a level a device expects, and a level to be raised or lowered, before slipping into metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个量长出四重身份：两点间的无形之差、表盘上的数字、设备期待的额定水平、可以升高的等级，最后进入比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a difference in level between two ends of a wire.
core.cn: 核心意象：导线两端之间的高差。

branches.en: The physics branch: the push between two points.
branches.cn: 物理分支：两点之间的推力。

branches.en: The reading branch: what the screen shows.
branches.cn: 读数分支：屏幕上显示的数。

branches.en: The rating branch: the level a lamp needs.
branches.cn: 额定分支：灯泡所需的水平。

branches.en: The transformer branch: raised or lowered on the way to a street.
branches.cn: 变压器分支：进入街道前被升高或降低。

branches.en: The metaphor branch: a band playing with real voltage.
branches.cn: 比喻分支：乐队演奏带着十足的劲头。

intro.en: Volt- names a unit and -age turns it into a quantity; compounds then describe where that quantity goes.
intro.cn: volt- 是一个单位名，-age 把它变成量，复合词再说明这个量往哪里去。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root for electricity is involved; the base is an Italian surname, and only the suffix is a Latin-descended ending.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有表示电的拉丁词根，基底是意大利姓氏，只有后缀是拉丁来源的词尾。

items.example: The volt is the base of the name.
items.exampleCN: volt 是这个名称的基底。

items.meaning: a fall from one level to another

items.example: Volt- carries the person, not a meaning.
items.exampleCN: volt- 携带的是人名而非意义。

items.example: The voltaic cell is named for Volta.
items.exampleCN: voltaic cell（伏打电池）以伏打命名。

definition_zh: 卷；册；体积；容积；音量
definition_en: a book forming part of a set, the amount of space something fills, or the loudness of a sound
core_image: 一册厚书与一杯水：一个占纸张的空间，一个占水的空间
scene: 深夜的图书馆里，管理员推着小车，把一册册合订本放回原位。She pulled a heavy volume from the shelf and opened it at the map.
sceneCN: 这里 volume 是「册、卷」（第 1 个义项：成套书中的一册）；句意为她从架上抽出一册厚重的书，翻到地图那一页。厚书占的那块空间，正是这个词的形象。

pos.zh: 卷；册；体积；容积；音量

derivatives.zh: 由 volume 加 -inous 构成，义为「多卷的；篇幅大的；宽松肥大的」
加 -etric 构成，义为「体积的；容积测量的」
加 -ly 构成，义为「大量地；宽松地」
同族形容词，义为「按体积计量的」

senses.title: A book as part of a set
senses.definition: a book, especially one of several that together make a complete work
senses.definitionCN: 一本书，尤指构成完整作品的若干册之一
senses.example: She pulled a heavy volume from the shelf and opened it at the map.
senses.exampleCN: 她从书架上抽出一册厚重的书，翻到地图那一页。
senses.why: Latin volumen meant a roll of writing, and a roll is one unit of a work; the sense of a single bound book grew straight from the roll.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 volumen 指书写的卷轴，一卷即作品的一个单位；「一册书」这一义项直接从卷轴长出来。

senses.title: The space something fills
senses.definition: the amount of three-dimensional space that a solid, liquid or gas takes up
senses.definitionCN: 固体、液体或气体所占的三维空间大小
senses.example: The box has twice the volume of the one beside it.
senses.exampleCN: 这个箱子的体积是旁边那个的两倍。
senses.why: A rolled manuscript takes up a rounded block of space; the same word was applied to the space any object occupies.
senses.whyCN: 卷起的书稿占着一块浑圆空间，同一个词便被用来指任何物体占的空间。

senses.title: The capacity of a container
senses.definition: the amount a container can hold, measured in litres or cubic units
senses.definitionCN: 容器能装下的量，以升或立方单位计
senses.example: The tank holds a volume of forty litres.
senses.exampleCN: 这只罐子的容积是四十升。
senses.why: The space an object occupies and the space a vessel can take are two sides of one measurement; the word keeps both.
senses.whyCN: 物体占的空间与容器能纳的空间是同一次度量的两面，这个词把两面都留下了。

senses.title: Loudness of sound
senses.definition: the degree of loudness of a sound, or the control that sets it
senses.definitionCN: 声音响亮的程度，或调节它的装置
senses.example: He turned the volume down when the baby fell asleep.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子睡着后他把音量调小。
senses.why: A sound fills a space the way a substance does; the more it fills, the louder it is, so the word moved to loudness.
senses.whyCN: 声音像物质一样填满空间，填得越满就越响，于是这个词转指音量。

senses.title: A quantity coming in large amounts
senses.definition: the amount of something produced, traded, or moving, often spoken of as large
senses.definitionCN: 生产、交易或流动的数量，常与「大量」连用
senses.example: The port handles a huge volume of goods each week.
senses.exampleCN: 这个港口每周处理大量货物。
senses.why: From a measured space the word extends to a measured quantity of anything that flows.
senses.whyCN: 从可量的空间出发，这个词扩展到任何流动之物的可量之数。

intro.en: Volume comes from Latin volumen, a roll of writing, from the verb volvere, to roll.
intro.cn: volume 来自拉丁语 volumen（书写的卷轴），源自动词 volvere（卷）。

items.en: Volvere meant to roll or to turn round, and volumen named a rolled sheet of writing.
items.cn: volvere 意为卷、转动，volumen 指卷起的书写纸张。

items.en: Old French volume carried the book sense into English in the medieval period.
items.cn: 古法语 volume 在中世纪把这个书义带入英语。

items.en: Early English volumes were still rolls, so book and bulk were one idea.
items.cn: 早期英语中的 volume 仍是卷轴，书与体积本是一个想法。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the physical sense of space filled grew separate and became the main scientific use.
items.cn: 十七世纪起，「填满的空间」这一物理义独立出来，成为主要科学用法。

items.en: Later uses added the loudness of sound and the amount of goods or traffic.
items.cn: 后来的用法又添上音量与货物、交通的数量。

note.en: The first group holds words of the same rolling root, the second the neighbouring measures and sound words.
note.cn: 第一组收同出「卷」这一词根的词，第二组收相近的度量与声音词。

entries.definition: The plural form of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词复数。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning consisting of many volumes, or very full and loose.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「多卷的、篇幅大的、宽松肥大的」。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning measured by volume.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「按体积计量的」。

entries.definition: A verb from the same rolling root, meaning to turn around.
entries.definitionCN: 同出「卷、转」词根的动词，义为「旋转」。

entries.definition: The amount a container can hold; close to sense three.
entries.definitionCN: 容器能容纳的量，近于第三个义项。

entries.definition: The general bigness of a thing, less technical than volume.
entries.definitionCN: 事物的总体大小，比 volume 少些技术色彩。

entries.definition: The plain word for how loud a sound is.
entries.definitionCN: 声音响亮程度的普通说法。

entries.definition: The everyday word for a bound text; volume is more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 装订成册读物的日常说法，volume 更正式。

normalIntro.en: Roll, fill, sound: one root covers a manuscript roll, a space, a tank and a dial.
normalIntro.cn: 卷、填、响：一个词根同时覆盖卷轴、空间、容器与旋钮。

normal.en: Volume and revolve share Latin volvere, to roll; a manuscript was rolled up.
normal.cn: volume 与 revolve 同出拉丁语 volvere（卷），手稿本是卷起来的。

normal.en: Volume of a box is length times width times height.
normal.cn: 箱子的体积等于长乘宽乘高。

normal.en: Turn up the volume is the everyday sound use.
normal.cn: turn up the volume 是音量义的日常说法。

normal.en: Voluminous means both many-volumed and loose-fitting.
normal.cn: voluminous 既指多卷的，也指宽松肥大的。

normal.en: The plural is plain volumes.
normal.cn: 复数是直接的 volumes。

abstract.en: Picture a scroll being rolled out on a table.
abstract.cn: 想一卷书稿在桌上被展开。

abstract.en: See a glass filling with water until it reaches the rim.
abstract.cn: 想一只杯子注水直到齐沿。

abstract.en: Hear a knob click softly as the music gets louder.
abstract.cn: 听旋钮轻响，音乐随之变大。

examples.en: The encyclopedia has twelve volumes.
examples.cn: 这部百科全书共有十二卷。

examples.en: Measure the volume of water in the tank.
examples.cn: 测量罐中水的体积。

examples.en: Please lower the volume after ten at night.
examples.cn: 夜里十点以后请把音量调低。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「窝柳木」——窝在柳木箱里的一卷书，箱子和书都占体积。

root: 拉丁语 volvere（卷、转动）→ volumen（卷轴）→ 古法语 volume → 英语 volume；由「卷」扩展到体积、容积、音量与数量。

sensesIntro.en: A roll grows into a book, then into the space a book takes, then into any filled space, then into a filled sound, then into any large amount.
sensesIntro.cn: 卷轴先长成一册书，再长成书占的空间、任何被填满的空间、被填满的声音，最后长成任何大量的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rolled manuscript and a filled vessel side by side.
core.cn: 核心意象：卷起的手稿与装满的容器并排放着。

branches.en: The book branch: the heavy volume opened at a map.
branches.cn: 书籍分支：翻到地图那一页的厚重一册。

branches.en: The space branch: a box twice the volume of another.
branches.cn: 空间分支：体积是另一个两倍的箱子。

branches.en: The container branch: a tank of forty litres.
branches.cn: 容器分支：容积四十升的罐子。

branches.en: The sound branch: turning the volume down.
branches.cn: 声音分支：把音量调小。

branches.en: The amount branch: goods passing through a port.
branches.cn: 数量分支：经过港口的货物。

intro.en: Vol- carries the rolling root, -um was the Latin noun ending, and English adds -inous, -etric and -s.
intro.cn: vol- 携带「卷」的词根，-um 是拉丁名词词尾，英语再加 -inous、-etric、-s。

latinIntro.en: Latin volvere and volumen are both recorded, as is the related noun voluta, a scroll of a column.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 volvere 与 volumen 均有记录，相关的 voluta（柱头涡卷）也有。

items.example: The root holds the rolling motion.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根携带滚卷的动作。

items.example: The verb also gives revolve and involve.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词还生出 revolve 与 involve。

items.example: The noun named the physical roll first.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词先指实物的卷轴。

items.example: The ending came intact into English.
It forms revolve from the same root.
items.exampleCN: 加在同一词根上构成 revolve。

items.example: It forms involve from the same root.
items.exampleCN: 加在同一词根上构成 involve。

definition_zh: 自愿的；志愿的；无偿的；有意的；随意的（动作）
definition_en: done or given because one chooses to, not because one is forced or paid
core_image: 一只手主动伸出去，没有绳子拉着它
scene: 社区公告栏前，一位退休教师写下自己的名字，报名周末辅导孩子。Her help at the centre was entirely voluntary.
sceneCN: 这里 voluntary 是「自愿的」（第 1 个义项：出于自己意愿而非被迫）；句意为她在中心的帮忙完全是自愿的。那只自己伸出去的手，就是这个词的形象。

pos.zh: 自愿的；志愿的；无偿的；随意的
（教堂音乐）仪式前或后的自愿短曲

derivatives.zh: 加 -ily 构成，义为「自愿地；主动地」
同根词，义为「志愿者；自愿者」
加 -ness 构成，义为「自愿性」
加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「非自愿的；不自觉的」

senses.title: Done by one's own choice
senses.definition: done, given or accepted freely, without being forced
senses.definitionCN: 自由地做出、给出或接受，而非被迫
senses.example: Her help at the centre was entirely voluntary.
senses.exampleCN: 她在中心的帮忙完全是自愿的。
senses.why: Latin voluntas is the will itself; voluntary describes an act that comes out of the will and nothing else.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 voluntas 就是「意志」本身，voluntary 形容的正是只出于意志、别无他力的行为。

senses.title: Work done without pay
senses.definition: of work or a worker, done without payment as a service
senses.definitionCN: 指工作或人，作为服务而不取报酬
senses.example: He does voluntary driving for the hospital twice a week.
senses.exampleCN: 他每周两次为医院做志愿接送。
senses.why: Latin voluntas is the will, and work done without pay is offered by the will alone.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 voluntas 是意志，不取报酬的工作正是只凭意志给出的。

senses.title: Not required by law or rule
senses.definition: allowed but not required, so that people may opt in
senses.definitionCN: 被允许但并非必须，人们可以选择加入
senses.example: The code of conduct is voluntary for small firms.
senses.exampleCN: 这套行为准则对小企业是非强制的。
senses.why: If a rule leaves the choice to the will, it can be joined freely and is therefore called voluntary.
senses.whyCN: 规定把选择权留给意志，人们可以自由加入，于是被称为自愿的。

senses.title: Movement under conscious control
senses.definition: of a muscle or movement, controlled by the will rather than automatic
senses.definitionCN: 指肌肉或动作，由意志控制而非自动发生
senses.example: Lifting your arm is a voluntary movement.
senses.exampleCN: 抬起手臂是一个随意动作。
senses.why: Physiology borrowed the word for muscles that obey the will, unlike the heart, which goes on by itself.
senses.whyCN: 生理学借这个词指听从意志的肌肉，与自行跳动的心脏不同。

senses.title: Done on purpose
senses.definition: in law and formal use, done deliberately rather than by accident
senses.definitionCN: 在法律与正式用语中，指有意为之而非出于意外
senses.example: The damage was voluntary, not an accident.
senses.exampleCN: 这处损坏是有意的，不是意外。
senses.why: An act done with the will behind it is deliberate; law keeps that link in this sense.
senses.whyCN: 背后有意志的行为就是有意的，法律在这一义项里保留了这层联系。

senses.title: A short organ piece in church
senses.titleCN: （教堂）仪式前后自愿演奏的短曲
senses.definition: a piece played on the organ before or after a service, offered at the player's choice
senses.definitionCN: 礼拜前后由演奏者自行选择的管风琴短曲
senses.example: The organist played a quiet voluntary as the church emptied.
senses.exampleCN: 教堂里的人散去时，管风琴师弹了一首安静的短曲。
senses.why: The piece was not part of the ordered service but was offered at the player's will, so it took the same name.
senses.whyCN: 这首曲子不在规定的礼拜程序之内，而是演奏者自愿给出的，于是借用了同一个名字。

intro.en: Voluntary rests on Latin voluntas, the will, which in turn comes from velle, to wish.
intro.cn: voluntary 建立在拉丁语 voluntas（意志）之上，后者又来自 velle（愿意）。

items.en: Velle meant to wish or to be willing, and voluntas named the will itself.
items.cn: velle 意为愿意、想要，voluntas 指意志本身。

items.en: Voluntarius described what was offered freely; Roman law already used it for acts done of one's own will.
items.cn: voluntarius 形容自由给予的东西，罗马法已用它指出于本人意愿的行为。

items.en: Old French volontaire carried the word to English.
items.cn: 古法语 volontaire 把这个词带进英语。

items.en: English kept the sense of free choice and added the sense of unpaid service.
items.cn: 英语保留了自由选择的含义，又添上无偿服务的含义。

items.en: Medicine borrowed the word for movements under conscious control, opposed to reflex.
items.cn: 医学借它指受意识控制的动作，与反射相对。

note.en: The first group gathers the will family, the second the words for chosen, unpaid and unwilling action.
note.cn: 第一组收「意志」词族，第二组收表示选择、无偿与不情愿的词。

entries.definition: The adverb, meaning of one's own free will.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「自愿地」。

entries.definition: A person who offers to help without pay.
entries.definitionCN: 无偿主动帮忙的人。

entries.definition: The quality of being voluntary.
entries.definitionCN: 自愿性。

entries.definition: Done without choice, such as a reflex.
entries.definitionCN: 非自愿的，如反射动作。

entries.definition: Free to be chosen or left out, by rule.
entries.definitionCN: 按规定可选可不选。

entries.definition: Done on purpose after thinking.
entries.definitionCN: 深思后有意为之。

entries.definition: Work for which no money is given.
entries.definitionCN: 不给报酬的工作。

entries.definition: Required by law or rule; the opposite of voluntary.
entries.definitionCN: 强制的，与 voluntary 相对。

normalIntro.en: Will is the whole root: every sense of voluntary is about an act with no outside hand.
normalIntro.cn: 「意志」就是全部词根：voluntary 的每个义项都指没有外力插手的行为。

normal.en: The Latin root is voluntas, the will.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根是 voluntas，意为「意志」。

normal.en: Voluntary and volunteer share that root.
normal.cn: voluntary 与 volunteer 共享这个词根。

normal.en: Voluntary work is unpaid and freely offered.
normal.cn: voluntary work 是不取报酬、自愿提供的工作。

normal.en: Voluntary muscle lifts the arm; involuntary muscle keeps the heart going.
normal.cn: 随意肌抬起手臂，不随意肌让心脏不停跳。

normal.en: The adverb is voluntarily, with a change of ending.
normal.cn: 副词是 voluntarily，词尾有变化。

abstract.en: See a hand reaching out with nothing pulling it.
abstract.cn: 想一只手自己伸出去，没有东西拉它。

abstract.en: Hear a coin dropped into a box that nobody forced you to fill.
abstract.cn: 听一枚硬币落入箱子，没人逼你投。

abstract.en: Picture a form where the box is left blank unless you choose to tick it.
abstract.cn: 想一张表格，除非你自愿打勾，否则那格空着。

examples.en: Attendance at the workshop is voluntary.
examples.cn: 参加工作坊是自愿的。

examples.en: She gave voluntary help to the new students.
examples.cn: 她主动帮助新生。

examples.en: Blinking is mostly an involuntary action, while waving is voluntary.
examples.cn: 眨眼大多是不自觉的动作，挥手则是随意的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我愿来」——我愿来就来，没人逼，这就是自愿。

root: 拉丁语 velle（愿意）→ voluntas（意志）→ voluntarius（自愿的）→ 古法语 volontaire → 英语 voluntary。

sensesIntro.en: One root, the will, spreads outward: free choice, unpaid service, rules one may join, movement one controls, intent in law, and a piece offered in church.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个「意志」词根向外铺开：自由选择、无偿服务、可加入的规定、受控的动作、法律中的故意，以及教堂里自愿演奏的曲子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching out with no rope attached.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只伸出却未被拴住的手。

branches.en: The choice branch: freely given help.
branches.cn: 选择分支：自愿给出的帮助。

branches.en: The unpaid branch: voluntary driving for a hospital.
branches.cn: 无偿分支：为医院做的志愿接送。

branches.en: The rule branch: a code that small firms may join.
branches.cn: 规则分支：小企业可以选择加入的准则。

branches.en: The control branch: a lifted arm, and damage done on purpose.
branches.cn: 控制分支：抬起的手臂与有意的损坏。

branches.en: The music branch: a quiet organ piece after service.
branches.cn: 音乐分支：礼拜后安静的管风琴短曲。

intro.en: Volunt- carries the will; -ary makes the adjective, and ordinary endings make the family.
intro.cn: volunt- 携带「意志」的含义，-ary 构成形容词，普通后缀再扩展出整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin velle, voluntas and voluntarius are all recorded, and so is the noun voluntas in legal texts.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 velle、voluntas、voluntarius 均有文献记录，voluntas 在法律文本中也常见。

items.example: The verb is the seed of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是词族的种子。

items.example: The noun is the base of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是形容词的基底。

definition_zh: 志愿者；志愿兵；自告奋勇者；自愿做；主动提供
definition_en: a person who freely offers to do something, especially without payment, or to offer oneself for a task
core_image: 人群中有人举起手，自己往前迈一步
scene: 洪水过后，社区大厅贴出招募告示，不到半天就挤满了人。Dozens of volunteers arrived with shovels before the rain stopped.
sceneCN: 这里 volunteer 是「志愿者」（第 1 个义项：自愿不计报酬做事的人）；句意为雨还没停，几十名志愿者就带着铁锹赶到了。人群中有人举手往前迈的那一步，正是这个词的形象。

pos.zh: 志愿者；志愿兵；自告奋勇者
自愿做；主动提供；自愿参军

collocations.zh: 自告奋勇承担这项任务

derivatives.zh: 同根形容词，义为「自愿的；无偿的」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「志愿服务；志愿活动」
同根副词，义为「自愿地」

senses.title: A person who offers to help
senses.definition: a person who offers to do something useful without being paid or forced
senses.definitionCN: 自愿不计报酬、也非被迫去做有益之事的人
senses.example: Dozens of volunteers arrived with shovels before the rain stopped.
senses.exampleCN: 雨还没停，几十名志愿者就带着铁锹赶到了。
senses.why: The noun comes from Latin voluntas, the will; a volunteer is someone whose coming depends on nothing but the will.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词来自拉丁语 voluntas（意志），volunteer 就是来与不来只看意志的人。

senses.title: To offer oneself for a task
senses.definition: to say that one is willing to do something, before being asked
senses.definitionCN: 在被要求之前就表示愿意去做
senses.example: She volunteered to drive the injured man to the clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 她自告奋勇开车送伤者去诊所。
senses.why: The verb turns the person into the action: stepping forward before anyone calls your name.
senses.whyCN: 动词把「人」变成「动作」：在有人点你的名字之前就跨前一步。

senses.title: To give information without being asked
senses.definition: to offer a remark or a piece of information freely, without a question
senses.definitionCN: 不经询问就主动说出看法或信息
senses.example: He volunteered a detail that the police had not asked about.
senses.exampleCN: 他主动说出一个警方并未问到的细节。
senses.why: Anything given without a request follows the same pattern: it is offered by the will, not pulled out by a question.
senses.whyCN: 凡未经请求就给出的东西都遵循同一模式：由意志主动给出，而非被问题拽出来。

senses.title: A soldier who serves by choice
senses.definition: a person who joins the armed forces by choice rather than by conscription
senses.definitionCN: 自愿入伍而非被征召的军人
senses.example: He served as a volunteer for three years before the war ended.
senses.exampleCN: 战争结束前他当了三年志愿兵。
senses.why: Armies once filled their ranks by force; a soldier who came freely stood out and took the same name as the helper.
senses.whyCN: 军队曾靠强制填补兵员，自愿前来的士兵格外显眼，于是与帮忙的人共用同一个名字。

senses.title: A plant growing without being sown
senses.definition: a plant that grows on its own from seed dropped by other plants
senses.definitionCN: 由别的植物落下的种子自己长出来的植物
senses.example: A volunteer appeared among the wheat and was left to grow.
senses.exampleCN: 麦田里冒出一株自生植物，被留着生长。
senses.why: Botany took the word for anything that arrives by itself, not planted by a hand.
senses.whyCN: 植物学借这个词指自己到来、并非人手栽种的东西。

intro.en: Volunteer came through French from Latin voluntarius, an adjective built on voluntas, the will.
intro.cn: volunteer 经法语来自拉丁语 voluntarius，这个形容词建立在 voluntas（意志）上。

items.en: Velle meant to wish, and voluntas named the will; voluntarius described what was done freely.
items.cn: velle 意为愿意，voluntas 指意志，voluntarius 形容自由做成的事。

items.en: French volunteer was first a soldier who offered to serve, and the military sense came first.
items.cn: 法语 volunte 原指自愿服役的士兵，军事义先出现。

items.en: English borrowed it in the sixteen hundreds for anyone who offered service.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入该词，泛指任何主动提供服务的人。

items.en: The verb followed the noun, first as to enlist and later as to offer anything freely.
items.cn: 动词随后跟上，先指自愿入伍，后指主动给出任何东西。

items.en: Modern gardening and botany added the plant that grows by itself.
items.cn: 现代园艺与植物学又添上自己长出来的植物义。

note.en: The first group holds the will family, the second the words for helpers and for service given.
note.cn: 第一组收「意志」词族，第二组收帮手与提供服务一类词。

entries.definition: The plural of the noun and the third person of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词复数，也是动词三单。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning done by free choice.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「自愿的」。

entries.definition: The adverb, meaning of one's own will.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「自愿地」。

entries.definition: The activity of giving unpaid service.
entries.definitionCN: 提供无偿服务的活动。

entries.definition: A person who helps; says nothing about being paid.
entries.definitionCN: 帮手，不涉及是否取酬。

entries.definition: A trainee gaining experience, sometimes unpaid but not voluntary.
entries.definitionCN: 实习者，有时不取酬但并非志愿性质。

entries.definition: Someone drawn in to join a force or a team.
entries.definitionCN: 被招募加入部队或团队的人。

entries.definition: A soldier forced to serve, the opposite of a volunteer.
entries.definitionCN: 被强征服役的士兵，与志愿兵相对。

normalIntro.en: The root is the will; the endings -eer and -ing just tell you who and what.
normalIntro.cn: 词根是「意志」，后缀 -eer 与 -ing 只说明是谁、是什么。

normal.en: Volunteer and voluntary share Latin voluntas, the will.
normal.cn: volunteer 与 voluntary 共享拉丁语 voluntas（意志）。

normal.en: The -eer ending names a person, as in engineer and mountaineer.
normal.cn: -eer 后缀指人，如 engineer、mountaineer。

normal.en: As a verb it takes an infinitive: volunteer to help.
normal.cn: 作动词时后接不定式：volunteer to help。

normal.en: A volunteer is not paid, but not every unpaid worker is a volunteer.
normal.cn: 志愿者不取报酬，但并非所有不取报酬的人都是志愿者。

normal.en: The plural volunteers does double duty for noun and verb.
normal.cn: 复数 volunteers 同时用作名词复数与动词三单。

abstract.en: See a hand go up in a crowd before anyone calls a name.
abstract.cn: 想人群中还没人点名，一只手已经举起。

abstract.en: Feel the one step forward that nobody ordered.
abstract.cn: 感受那一步没人命令却自己迈出的向前。

abstract.en: Picture a high-visibility vest with no name tag, only a willingness.
abstract.cn: 想一件没有名牌的高亮背心，只写着「愿意」。

examples.en: Each volunteer was given a map and a bottle of water.
examples.cn: 每位志愿者都领到一张地图和一瓶水。

examples.en: Nobody asked him, but he volunteered to carry the boxes.
examples.cn: 没人叫他，他却主动去搬箱子。

examples.en: The school needs volunteers to read with young children.
examples.cn: 学校需要志愿者陪小朋友读书。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我愿提尔」——我愿提着尔的东西跑一趟，这就是志愿者。

root: 拉丁语 velle（愿意）→ voluntas（意志）→ 中世纪拉丁语 voluntarius → 法语 volunte（自愿入伍者）→ 英语 volunteer。

sensesIntro.en: The will becomes a person, then an action, then any freely given remark, then a freely enlisted soldier, then a plant that plants itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 意志先变成一个人，再变成一个动作、一句主动说出的话、一名自愿入伍的兵，最后一株自己长出来的植物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand raised before anyone asks.
core.cn: 核心意象：还没人开口就举起的手。

branches.en: The person branch: people with shovels in the rain.
branches.cn: 人物分支：雨中拿铁锹的人们。

branches.en: The action branch: volunteering to drive someone to a clinic.
branches.cn: 动作分支：主动开车送人去诊所。

branches.en: The remark branch: a detail nobody asked for.
branches.cn: 言语分支：没人问就说出一个细节。

branches.en: The army branch: three years of free service.
branches.cn: 军队分支：三年自愿服役。

branches.en: The plant branch: a stalk among the wheat.
branches.cn: 植物分支：麦田里的那一株。

intro.en: Volunt- is the will, -eer names a person, and -ing turns the verb into an activity.
intro.cn: volunt- 是「意志」，-eer 指人，-ing 把动词变成活动。

latinIntro.en: Latin voluntas and voluntarius are recorded, and French volunte stands between them and the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 voluntas 与 voluntarius 均有记录，法语 volunte 夹在它们与英语词之间。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根携带「自由选择」之义。
它构成 volunteer 与 engineer。

items.meaning: more than one, or he does

items.example: It forms conscript, the opposite idea.
items.exampleCN: 它与 scribe 构成 conscript，表示相反的意思。

items.example: It forms recruit, a related word.
items.exampleCN: 它与 cruit 构成相关的 recruit。

items.example: A volunteer does what shall never forced.
items.exampleCN: 志愿者做的是从未被强求的事。

definition_zh: 投票；表决；选票；选举权；投票决定
definition_en: to choose in an election or a meeting by marking a paper or raising a hand, or the choice so made
core_image: 一张折好的纸条被投进木箱，箱口缝着锁
scene: 社区中心的长桌旁排着队，每人领到一张纸，走进布帘后面。After a short debate, the committee voted to move the meeting to Friday.
sceneCN: 这里 vote 是「投票表决」（第 1 个义项：用票或举手做出选择）；句意为简短讨论后，委员会投票决定把会议改到周五。纸条落进木箱的那一刻，就是这个词的核心画面。

pos.zh: 投票；表决；选票；选举权；投票权
投票；表决；投票决定；投票通过

derivatives.zh: 由 vote 加 -er 构成，义为「选民；投票人」
加 -ing 构成，义为「投票行为；表决」
同义相关的名词，义为「全体选民」
同出 votum 词根的词，义为「奉献；致力于」

senses.title: To choose by marking or raising a hand
senses.definition: to make a formal choice in an election or a meeting
senses.definitionCN: 在选举或会议上做出正式选择
senses.example: After a short debate, the committee voted to move the meeting to Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 简短讨论后，委员会投票决定把会议改到周五。
senses.why: Latin votum was a vow, a solemn promise to a god; the choice of a ruler was once made by public promise, and the word slid from promising to choosing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 votum 是誓言、对神的郑重许诺；推举首领原是通过公开表态完成，这个词便从「许诺」滑向「选择」。

senses.title: The paper or the choice itself
senses.definition: the ballot used, or the recorded choice, as in one vote each
senses.definitionCN: 所用的选票或记录下的选择，如每人一票
senses.example: The result was thirty votes to twelve.
senses.exampleCN: 结果是三十票对十二票。
senses.why: Once the act had a name, the count of the acts took the same word: a pile of paper choices is a number of votes.
senses.whyCN: 行为一旦有了名字，行为的计数也用同一个词：一堆纸上的选择就是若干张选票。

senses.title: The right to take part
senses.definition: the legal right of a person to take part in an election
senses.definitionCN: 一个人参加选举的法定权利
senses.example: The movement won the vote for women in the nineteen twenties.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动为女性争取到了选举权。
senses.why: A right is spoken of as the thing it allows, so the right to cast a vote is simply called the vote.
senses.whyCN: 权利常以它所允许之事来称呼，于是投一票的权利就被简称为 the vote。

senses.title: To agree or pass formally
senses.definition: of a body, to agree by voting, as in voting money for a project
senses.definitionCN: 指机构经表决同意，如投票拨款给某项目
senses.example: Parliament voted a sum for the new bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 议会表决通过为新桥拨款。
senses.why: A decision made by vote carries the force of the group, so the verb also expresses what the vote has settled.
senses.whyCN: 表决作出的决定带着集体的效力，动词于是也表达表决已定下的事。

senses.title: To declare strongly
senses.definition: in informal use, to say with general agreement, as in this was voted the best film
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示众人一致认为，如被评为最佳影片
senses.example: The little cafe was voted the best in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这家小咖啡馆被评为全城最佳。
senses.why: A praise decided by many voices is settled the way an election is, so the vote verb stretches to shared opinion.
senses.whyCN: 由众人之声决定的好评也像选举一样定下来，于是 vote 这一动词又扩展到共同看法。

intro.en: Vote comes from Latin votum, a vow, from the verb vovere, to promise or to wish.
intro.cn: vote 来自拉丁语 votum（誓言），源自动词 vovere（许诺、祈愿）。

items.en: Vovere meant to promise solemnly or to wish, often in a religious setting.
items.cn: vovere 意为郑重许诺或祈愿，常用于宗教场合。

items.en: Votum named the promise itself, and the plural vota named things promised to a god.
items.cn: votum 指许诺本身，复数 vota 指许给神的东西。

items.en: In the Middle Ages votum was used for a formal expression of opinion in an assembly.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语中，votum 被用来指会议里正式表达意见。

items.en: English took the word in the fifteenth century for the formal choice made in a meeting.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪引入该词，指会议中做出的正式选择。

items.en: Modern democracy widened it to ballots, to the right to choose, and to the count of voices.
items.cn: 现代民主制把它扩展到选票、选择权与票数。

note.en: The first group gives words on the same vow root, the second the words used around an election.
note.cn: 第一组是同一「誓言」词根的词，第二组是选举场景中常用的词。

entries.definition: A person who votes in an election.
entries.definitionCN: 在选举中投票的人。

entries.definition: The act of choosing, often used before another noun.
entries.definitionCN: 投票行为，常置于名词前。

entries.definition: From the vow root, meaning to give oneself completely.
entries.definitionCN: 同出「誓言」词根，义为「奉献」。

entries.definition: The English companion of the Latin noun, still meaning a solemn promise.
entries.definitionCN: 与拉丁名词同源的英语词，仍指庄严许诺。

entries.definition: To choose a person for office, and a formal process around the choice.
entries.definitionCN: 选出任职者，强调选举过程。

entries.definition: The paper used and the system of secret voting.
entries.definitionCN: 所用的选票与无记名投票制度。

entries.definition: The counting of votes, or a survey of opinions.
entries.definitionCN: 计票；或民意调查。

entries.definition: The everyday word for picking one thing instead of another.
entries.definitionCN: 从中挑选的日常说法。

normalIntro.en: A vow became a choice: vot- carries the promise, and short English endings do the rest.
normalIntro.cn: 誓言变成了选择：vot- 携带「许诺」，其余交给简短的英语词尾。

normal.en: Vote and vow share the Latin root votum, a vow.
normal.cn: vote 与 vow 共享拉丁词根 votum（誓言）。

normal.en: Vote for, vote against, vote on a plan: three prepositions to learn.
normal.cn: vote for、vote against、vote on a plan：三个介词要分清。

normal.en: Cast a vote and cast a ballot say the same thing.
normal.cn: cast a vote 与 cast a ballot 意思相同。

normal.en: A voter votes; the voting lasts for hours.
normal.cn: a voter 投票，the voting 持续数小时。

normal.en: Devote has the same root: to vow yourself to a cause.
normal.cn: devote 同根：把自己许诺给某个事业。

abstract.en: See a folded paper slipping into a locked box.
abstract.cn: 想一张折好的纸滑进锁着的木箱。

abstract.en: Hear hands go up one by one in a quiet hall.
abstract.cn: 听安静的大厅里一只手一只手举起来。

abstract.en: Feel the small weight of one paper among thousands.
abstract.cn: 感受成千上万张纸里那一张的分量。

examples.en: Many people voted early this year.
examples.cn: 今年很多人提前投了票。

examples.en: Each member has one vote in the committee.
examples.cn: 每位成员在委员会中都有一次投票权。

examples.en: They voted him out after only a year.
examples.cn: 仅仅一年之后，他们就投票让他下台了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「沃特」——沃特把票投进箱里，举手说：我投这一票。

root: 拉丁语 vovere（许诺、祈愿）→ votum（誓言）→ 中世纪拉丁语 votum（表决意见）→ 英语 vote。

sensesIntro.en: A vow becomes a choice, the choice becomes a paper, the paper count becomes a number, the right grows around it, and finally the whole group agrees.
sensesIntro.cn: 誓言先变成选择，选择变成一张纸，纸的计数变成数字，周围长出权利，最后整群人以投票共认。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one folded paper going into a box.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张折好的纸投进木箱。

branches.en: The act branch: a committee deciding by vote.
branches.cn: 行为分支：委员会以投票作决定。

branches.en: The paper branch: thirty votes to twelve.
branches.cn: 票纸分支：三十票对十二票。

branches.en: The right branch: the vote for women.
branches.cn: 权利分支：女性的选举权。

branches.en: The settlement branch: voting money for a bridge.
branches.cn: 决议分支：表决通过拨款造桥。

branches.en: The opinion branch: voted the best cafe in town.
branches.cn: 评价分支：被评为全城最佳咖啡馆。

intro.en: Vot- carries the vow; -er, -ing, -e and -ed are all ordinary English endings.
intro.cn: vot- 携带「誓言」之义，-er、-ing、-e、-ed 都是普通英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin vovere and votum are both recorded, so this root is secure.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vovere 与 votum 都有文献记录，这个词根是可靠的。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根携带「许诺」之义。

items.example: The verb gives devote as well.
The noun is the direct source.

items.meaning: more than one, or he does

items.example: It forms devote from the same root.
items.exampleCN: 加在同一词根上构成 devote。

items.example: It forms the rare ab-vote idea of casting off a vow.
items.exampleCN: 它与该词根构成罕见的「弃誓」义。

items.example: A ballot is the paper, a vote is the choice.
items.exampleCN: ballot 指那张纸，vote 指那个选择。

definition_zh: 工资；报酬；发动（战争）；进行（斗争）
definition_en: money paid to a worker for work done, usually hourly or daily, or to carry on a war or a campaign
core_image: 一周的工时记在纸上，换成一叠按周发的钱
scene: 工厂门口的告示牌上写着新的时薪，工人们围着看了很久。The workers asked for a higher wage and shorter hours.
sceneCN: 这里 wage 是「工资」（第 1 个义项：按工计酬的钱，常按周或按小时发）；句意为工人们要求提高工资、缩短工时。那块写着时薪的告示牌，就是这个词的日常画面。

pos.zh: 工资；报酬；（复数）代价
发动（战争）；进行（斗争）；开展（运动）

derivatives.zh: 复数形式，常指一笔工资，也指「报应、代价」
同形近词，义为「赌注；打赌」，来源不同
复合词，义为「挣工资的人；工薪族」

senses.title: Money paid for work
senses.definition: money paid regularly to a worker, usually for hours or days worked
senses.definitionCN: 按工时或工日定期付给工人的钱
senses.example: The workers asked for a higher wage and shorter hours.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们要求提高工资、缩短工时。
senses.why: The word began as a promise to pay, from a Germanic root for a pledge; a wage is money promised for work.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原指「许诺付给的报酬」，源自日耳曼语表示「抵押、许诺」的词根，所以 wage 就是为工作许诺付的钱。

senses.title: The plural as a sum or a price
senses.definition: the plural wages for the money as a whole, or for what a deed finally costs
senses.definitionCN: 复数 wages 指整笔工资，也指某行为的最终代价
senses.example: The wages of that carelessness were heavy.
senses.exampleCN: 那次疏忽的代价很沉重。
senses.why: A sum of money owed for work became a general image of what any action finally pays out.
senses.whyCN: 为工作应付的一笔钱，进而成了任何行为最终「付出的钱」的普遍比喻。

senses.title: To carry on a war
senses.definition: to begin and continue a war or a long struggle
senses.definitionCN: 开始并持续进行战争或长期斗争
senses.example: The two states waged war for nearly a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 两国交战将近十年。
senses.why: The old verb meant to pledge oneself to a fight; to wage war is to put that pledge into action.
senses.whyCN: 旧时动词义为「以自己为质投入战斗」，wage war 就是把这份许诺付诸行动。

senses.title: To carry on a campaign
senses.definition: to conduct a long public effort, as a campaign against disease
senses.definitionCN: 长期进行某种公众努力，如对抗疾病的运动
senses.example: The town waged a long campaign for clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 全镇为清洁水源开展了长期运动。
senses.why: From war the verb widened to any sustained struggle that must be carried on over time.
senses.whyCN: 从战争出发，动词扩展到任何需要长期坚持的斗争。

senses.title: To bet or stake
senses.definition: in older use, to stake money on a result
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法中，拿钱赌一个结果
senses.example: He wagered his whole month's pay on one race.
senses.exampleCN: 他把整月的工钱全押在一场比赛上。
senses.why: The staking sense came through wager from the same root of pledge; here a promise is put at risk.
senses.whyCN: 下注义经 wager 从同一「抵押、许诺」词根而来，此时许诺被置于风险之中。

intro.en: Wage comes from a Germanic root meaning a pledge or a stake, borrowed through Old French.
intro.cn: wage 来自日耳曼语表示「抵押、许质」的词根，经古法语借入英语。

items.en: The root behind wage meant a pledge or a sum put up as security.
items.cn: wage 背后的词根意为抵押或许诺的保证金。

items.en: Old French wage and gage carried the idea of a pledge into France.
items.cn: 古法语 wage 与 gage 把「抵押」的观念带进法国。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the middle ages as a payment promised for service.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪借入该词，指为服役许诺的报酬。

items.en: A verb to wage battle grew beside it, meaning to put oneself up as pledge for a fight.
items.cn: 旁边长出动词 wage battle，意为以自身作质投入战斗。

items.en: Modern use split the pair: wage as regular pay, and wage a war or a campaign.
items.cn: 现代用法分作两支：wage 作定期工资，以及 wage a war 或 wage a campaign。

note.en: The first group holds the words that look or sound close, the second the words for pay and pay-related actions.
note.cn: 第一组收形近音近词，第二组收与报酬及开战相关的词。

entries.definition: The plural, often meaning pay as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 复数，常指整笔工资。

entries.definition: A bet, from the same pledge root but a different path.
entries.definitionCN: 赌注，同出「抵押」词根但路径不同。

entries.definition: The past tense of the verb, as in waged a campaign.
entries.definitionCN: 动词过去式，如 waged a campaign。

entries.definition: To move a tail from side to side; unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 摇尾巴，与此词无关。

entries.definition: Pay stated as a yearly sum, usually monthly.
entries.definitionCN: 按年额计、通常按月发的报酬。

entries.definition: The everyday word covering all kinds of payment.
entries.definitionCN: 各类报酬的日常统称。

entries.definition: All money coming in, from work and other sources.
entries.definitionCN: 收入，包括劳动与其他来源。

entries.definition: Money gained by work, often over a period.
entries.definitionCN: 劳动所得，常按一段时间计。

normalIntro.en: A pledge gives both a salary and a war: what is promised for work, and what is staked in a fight.
normalIntro.cn: 「许诺」同时生出工资与战争：为工作许诺的报酬，为战斗押上的本身。

normal.en: Wage is pay for hours or days; salary is a yearly figure paid monthly.
normal.cn: wage 按小时或工日计，salary 按年额按月发。

normal.en: The plural wages means the pay as a whole, not many salaries.
normal.cn: 复数 wages 指整笔工资，不是很多份工资。

normal.en: Wage a war, wage a campaign: the verb needs a struggle after it.
normal.cn: wage a war、wage a campaign：这个动词后面要接斗争。

normal.en: Wag is a different word: a dog wags its tail.
normal.cn: wag 是另一个词：狗摇尾巴。

normal.en: The minimum wage is the legal floor for hourly pay.
normal.cn: the minimum wage 是时薪的法定下限。

abstract.en: See a paper slip of hours turning into cash on a Friday.
abstract.cn: 想一张工时单在周五变成现金。

abstract.en: Hear coins counted out on a wooden counter.
abstract.cn: 听硬币在木柜台上被数出来。

abstract.en: Feel a promise made before the work even began.
abstract.cn: 感受工作在开始前就已给出的许诺。

examples.en: His weekly wage barely covers the rent.
examples.cn: 他的周薪勉强够付房租。

examples.en: The union fought for a fair wage.
examples.cn: 工会为公平的工资而斗争。

examples.en: The country waged a long war over water rights.
examples.cn: 这个国家为水权打了很久的仗。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「胃哥」——胃哥干活最卖力，只为月底那笔工资。

root: 日耳曼语 *wadi-（抵押、许诺）→ 古法语 wage/gage → 英语 wage（工资）；同根并生动词义「发动战争」。

sensesIntro.en: A pledge stretches in two directions: money promised for work, and oneself pledged to a struggle.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个「许诺」向两个方向伸展：为工作许诺的钱，以及把自己押上的斗争。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a paper of hours exchanged for cash.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张工时单换成一笔现金。

branches.en: The pay branch: a demand for higher hourly pay.
branches.cn: 报酬分支：要求提高时薪。

branches.en: The price branch: the wages of carelessness.
branches.cn: 代价分支：疏忽的代价。

branches.en: The war branch: two states waging war for a decade.
branches.cn: 战争分支：两国交战十年。

branches.en: The campaign branch: a town fighting for clean water.
branches.cn: 运动分支：全镇为清洁水源而奋斗。

branches.en: The stake branch: a month of pay on one race.
branches.cn: 下注分支：一个月的工钱押在一场比赛上。

intro.en: Wage has no productive prefix; the family is made of the plural -es, the past -ed and a few compounds.
intro.cn: wage 没有能产的词缀，词族由复数 -es、过去式 -ed 和少量复合词构成。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic, not Latin; it reached English through Old French, so no Latin entry is given.
latinIntro.cn: 词根为日耳曼语而非拉丁语，经古法语进入英语，故不列拉丁词条。

items.example: The root gives both pay and warfare.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根同时生出报酬与战争。

items.example: The spelling settled with a final e.
items.exampleCN: 拼写最终带一个不发音的 e。

items.meaning: more than one, or he does

items.exampleCN: 它构成 wager 与 wage-earner。

definition_zh: 腰；腰部；（衣服的）腰身；腰围
definition_en: the part of the body between the ribs and the hips, or the part of a garment that fits around it
core_image: 两手叉在身体中段，那里最窄也最能弯
scene: 裁缝绕着她的腰量了一圈，把数字写在纸样边上。The coat was taken in at the waist so that it fitted better.
sceneCN: 这里 waist 是「腰部」（第 1 个义项：肋骨与胯之间的身体部分）；句意为大衣在腰部收窄，以便更合身。两手叉腰的那处身体中段，就是这个词的形象。

pos.zh: 腰；腰部；腰身；腰围

derivatives.zh: waist 与 coat 复合，义为「马甲」
waist 与 band 复合，义为「腰带；裤腰」
waist 与 line 复合，义为「腰线；腰围」
加 -ed 构成，常与形容词连用，如 high-waisted「高腰的」

senses.title: The middle of the body
senses.definition: the narrow middle part of the body between the chest and the hips
senses.definitionCN: 身体在胸与胯之间较窄的中段
senses.example: The coat was taken in at the waist so that it fitted better.
senses.exampleCN: 大衣在腰部收窄，以便更合身。
senses.why: The old word meant growth, then the place where a body grows and bends; the middle of the trunk took the name.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的旧义是「生长」，随后指身体生长弯曲之处，躯干的中段便得了这个名字。

senses.title: The part of a garment there
senses.definition: the part of a dress, skirt or trousers that sits around the waist
senses.definitionCN: 裙、裤等衣服围绕腰部的那一部分
senses.example: The skirt has a wide waist with a hidden zip.
senses.exampleCN: 这条裙子腰身宽松，还藏着一个拉链。
senses.why: A garment copies the body it covers, so the middle seam of a dress is simply called the waist.
senses.whyCN: 衣服照抄它所包住的身体，裙子的中段接缝就被直接称为 waist。

senses.title: The measurement around it
senses.definition: the measurement of the body at that narrow point
senses.definitionCN: 在身体最窄处量出的周长
senses.example: His waist has not changed in twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他的腰围二十年没有变化。
senses.why: A size is quoted as the measurement of a part, so clothes are sold by waist as well as by chest.
senses.whyCN: 尺码常以某部位的测量值表示，所以衣服既按胸围也按腰围出售。

senses.title: The narrow middle of a thing
senses.definition: the narrower middle of a ship, an object or a shape
senses.definitionCN: 船体、器物或形状较窄的中段
senses.example: The ship was struck just forward of the waist.
senses.exampleCN: 船在腰段稍前处被击中。
senses.why: Any long body that swells at the ends and narrows in the middle can borrow the name of the human waist.
senses.whyCN: 任何两端粗、中间窄的长形物都可借用人腰的名字。

senses.title: The middle section of a violin family
senses.definition: the inward-curved middle of the body of a violin or a guitar
senses.definitionCN: 小提琴或吉他琴身向内收的中段
senses.example: The maker cut the waist of the instrument by hand.
senses.exampleCN: 制琴师手工把琴身的中腰挖出来。
senses.why: Instrument makers named the curved middle after the body, because the curve lets the bow move freely across the strings.
senses.whyCN: 制琴师按人体给这个弯中段命名，因为这段弯曲让弓能自由过弦。

intro.en: Waist goes back to a Germanic word for growth, which then named the growing middle of the body.
intro.cn: waist 上溯到日耳曼语表示「生长」的词，随后指身体生长、弯折的中段。

items.en: The root meant to grow, and the noun meant growth or increase.
items.cn: 词根意为生长，名词义为生长、增加。

items.en: Old English wæstm is recorded meaning growth, a fruit or a produce.
items.cn: 古英语 wæstm 有记录，义为生长、果实或收成。

items.en: The sense narrowed to the body's growing part, then to the narrow middle between ribs and hips.
items.cn: 词义缩到身体的生长部位，再缩到肋骨与胯之间的窄中段。

items.en: Tailoring took it over for the fitting part of a garment and for the size sold by it.
items.cn: 裁缝业借它指衣服合身的那一段，以及据它出售的尺码。

items.en: Shipbuilders and violin makers extended it to the narrow middle of what they make.
items.cn: 造船与制琴把它扩展到所造之物较窄的中段。

note.en: The first group follows the family and a common homophone, the second the neighbouring words for the body and for clothes.
note.cn: 第一组收同族词与常见同音词，第二组收身体与衣着的邻近词。

entries.definition: The plural of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词复数。

entries.definition: A different word meaning loss or rubbish, with the same sound.
entries.definitionCN: 同音异义词，义为浪费、废物。

entries.definition: The band of cloth around the top of trousers.
entries.definitionCN: 裤子顶部的腰围布带。

entries.definition: The line of the waist, and the measurement at it.
entries.definitionCN: 腰线，以及腰围尺寸。

entries.definition: The joint beside and below the waist.
entries.definitionCN: 腰侧下方的髋部。

entries.definition: The front of the body between chest and waist.
entries.definitionCN: 胸与腰之间的腹部前面。

entries.definition: The strap worn around the waist.
entries.definitionCN: 系在腰上的带子。

entries.definition: The trunk of the body, of which the waist is the narrow part.
entries.definitionCN: 躯干，腰是其中较窄的一段。

normalIntro.en: One short word, four long compounds, and one homophone to keep apart.
normalIntro.cn: 一个短词、四个复合词，以及一个必须分开的同音词。

normal.en: Waste and waist sound alike but waste is loss, waist is the body.
normal.cn: waste 与 waist 同音，但 waste 是浪费，waist 是身体部位。

normal.en: Compounds keep the spelling: waistcoat, waistband, waistline.
normal.cn: 复合词保留拼写：waistcoat、waistband、waistline。

normal.en: A waistcoat is a garment at the waist, a vest in American use.
normal.cn: waistcoat 是穿在腰部的衣物，美式称 vest。

normal.en: Tailored clothes are taken in at the waist.
normal.cn: 定制的衣服在腰部收窄。

normal.en: A violin has a waist because its sides curve inwards.
normal.cn: 小提琴有腰身，因为两侧向内弯。

abstract.en: Picture hands on the narrowest part of the body.
abstract.cn: 想两只手叉在身体最窄处。

abstract.en: See a ribbon tied around the middle of a parcel.
abstract.cn: 想一条丝带扎在包裹的中段。

abstract.en: Feel the inward curve of a guitar against your knee.
abstract.cn: 感受吉他的内弯贴在膝上。

examples.en: She tied the apron around her waist.
examples.cn: 她把围裙系在腰上。

examples.en: The water came up to his waist.
examples.cn: 水没到他的腰部。

examples.en: This dress is loose at the waist.
examples.cn: 这条裙子腰部较松。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「围丝」——用丝带围在腰上的那圈，就是腰部。

root: 日耳曼语 *wahs-（生长）→ 古英语 wæstm（生长、果实）→ 中古英语 waist（身体中段）→ 现代英语 waist。

sensesIntro.en: Growth narrows into the middle of the body, then spreads out again into clothes, sizes, ships and violins.
sensesIntro.cn: 「生长」先缩成身体中段，再向外铺开成衣服、尺码、船体与提琴的腰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands on the narrow middle of the body.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手叉在身体较窄的中段。

branches.en: The body branch: a coat taken in at the waist.
branches.cn: 身体分支：腰部收窄的大衣。

branches.en: The clothing branch: a skirt with a wide waist.
branches.cn: 衣着分支：腰身宽松的裙子。

branches.en: The size branch: a waist unchanged for twenty years.
branches.cn: 尺码分支：二十年不变的腰围。

branches.en: The object branch: the waist of a ship.
branches.cn: 器物分支：船的中腰。

branches.en: The instrument branch: the curved waist of a violin.
branches.cn: 乐器分支：小提琴内弯的中腰。

intro.en: Waist- already carries the body meaning; the compounds add coat, band, line and a past ending.
intro.cn: waist- 本身已带身体义，复合词再加 coat、band、line 与过去式词尾。

latinIntro.en: This root is Germanic; it has no Latin ancestor, so the entry lists no Latin word.
latinIntro.cn: 该词根为日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先，故不列拉丁词条。

items.example: The noun is the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是词族的基底。

definition_zh: 等；等候；等待；（旧）埋伏；（英）侍奉
definition_en: to stay somewhere or hold back from acting until something happens
core_image: 一个人站在门口，眼睛盯着路的尽头
scene: 雨天的公交站台上，几个人缩着肩，不时探头看远处的车灯。We waited nearly an hour for the last bus to come.
sceneCN: 这里 wait 是「等候」（第 1 个义项：留在原处直到某事发生）；句意为为了最后一班车，我们等了将近一小时。站在站台上盯着路尽头的那副样子，就是这个词的形象。

pos.zh: 等；等候；等待；推迟
等待；等候的时间

derivatives.zh: wait 加 -er 构成，义为「侍者；服务员」
waiter 加 -ess 构成，义为「女服务员」
加 -ing 构成，义为「等待」
a- 与 wait 复合，义为「等候（某事）」

senses.title: To stay until something happens
senses.definition: to stay in a place or delay action until something expected happens
senses.definitionCN: 留在某处或推迟行动，直到期待之事发生
senses.example: We waited nearly an hour for the last bus to come.
senses.exampleCN: 为了最后一班车，我们等了将近一小时。
senses.why: The word came from a Germanic verb meaning to watch or to keep guard; a watcher stands still and that is what a waiter does.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自日耳曼语动词，意为观望、守候；观望的人站着不动，等待之人正是如此。

senses.title: To delay something
senses.definition: to put off doing something until a later moment
senses.definitionCN: 把某事推到稍后再做
senses.example: Wait until the paint is dry before you touch it.
senses.exampleCN: 等漆干了再碰。
senses.why: If you stand guard you do nothing for a while, so the verb also means to hold an action back.
senses.whyCN: 守候的人有一阵子什么都不做，于是动词也指把行动按住。

senses.title: To be ready to serve
senses.definition: in the older use, to attend on someone or to serve at table
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法指在旁伺候，或侍奉餐桌
senses.example: He waited at table in the evenings to pay for his studies.
senses.exampleCN: 他晚上在餐桌旁伺候，以支付学费。
senses.why: A servant waits, meaning attends nearby and watches for a sign; the waiter of a restaurant still carries that meaning.
senses.whyCN: 仆役「候着」，即在一旁看着等吩咐；餐厅的侍者仍带着这层意思。

senses.title: To lie in ambush
senses.definition: in older use, to lie hidden and watch for a chance to strike
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法指藏起来，等机会出手
senses.example: The hunters waited in the reeds for the birds to land.
senses.exampleCN: 猎人们藏在芦苇里等鸟落下。
senses.why: The original sense of watching has a dark side: a watcher may be hidden and watching for prey.
senses.whyCN: 观望的本义有一个阴暗面：观望者也可能藏着看猎物。

senses.title: A period of waiting
senses.definition: the time spent waiting, or the act of waiting itself
senses.definitionCN: 等待所花的时间，或等待这一行为
senses.example: There was a long wait before the results were announced.
senses.exampleCN: 结果公布之前有一段漫长的等待。
senses.why: The noun turns the act into a stretch of time that can be counted or complained about.
senses.whyCN: 名词把这一行为变成一段可以计数、可以抱怨的时间。

senses.title: The phrase wait and see
senses.definition: in the fixed phrase, to take no action and watch how things turn out
senses.definitionCN: 固定说法里指暂不行动，看事情如何发展
senses.example: The doctor said we should wait and see for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 医生说我们先观察一周再说。
senses.why: Watching and holding back are the two halves of the verb; the phrase puts both together.
senses.whyCN: 观望与按住正是这个动词的两半，这个短语把两半合在一起。

intro.en: Wait comes from a Germanic verb meaning to watch or to keep guard, borrowed through Old French.
intro.cn: wait 来自日耳曼语表示观望、守候的动词，经古法语借入英语。

items.en: A Germanic root for watching produced a verb meaning keep guard.
items.cn: 日耳曼语表示观望的词根产生了一个意为守候的动词。

items.en: Old French waitier or guaitier meant to watch, and to lie in wait.
items.cn: 古法语 waitier 或 guaitier 意为观望，也指埋伏。

items.en: English borrowed the word as a verb of watching and ambush in the north of France.
items.cn: 英语在法国北部方言中借入这个词，用于观望与埋伏。

items.en: The sense shifted to staying still for an expected event, which is now the main meaning.
items.cn: 词义转到为期待之事留在原处，这成为今天的主要含义。

items.en: Service at table kept a separate sense, and the noun waiter came from it.
items.cn: 侍奉餐桌保留了另一支义项，名词 waiter 由此而来。

note.en: The first group holds the family and the look-alike, the second the words for staying and for expecting.
note.cn: 第一组收同族词与形近词，第二组收停留与预期的近义词。

entries.definition: The third person of the verb and the plural of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 动词三单与名词复数。

entries.definition: The past tense and past participle.
entries.definitionCN: 过去式与过去分词。

entries.definition: A different word for heaviness, with the same sound.
entries.definitionCN: 同音异义词，义为重量。

entries.definition: A formal verb meaning to wait for, used without a preposition.
entries.definitionCN: 正式动词，义为等候，后面不再加 for。

entries.definition: To think something will happen, without staying in place.
entries.definitionCN: 认为某事会发生，不必留在原处。

entries.definition: To put something off, often without intending to.
entries.definitionCN: 推迟某事，常非出于自愿。

entries.definition: To stay on longer than needed, without a clear purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 逗留过久，目的不明。

entries.definition: To remain in a place, whether or not one is waiting.
entries.definitionCN: 留在某处，不一定在等。

normalIntro.en: Watch, then stand, then serve: the whole family grows from keeping an eye on something.
normalIntro.cn: 先是观望，再是站着，最后是伺候：整个词族都从「盯着看」长出来。

normal.en: Wait for someone, but await someone: await takes no for.
normal.cn: wait for someone，但 await someone：await 后面不加 for。

normal.en: Wait is also a noun: there was a long wait at the airport.
normal.cn: wait 也是名词：在机场等了很久。

normal.en: Waiter and waitress come from waiting at table.
normal.cn: waiter 与 waitress 来自在餐桌旁伺候。

normal.en: Weight sounds the same and means heaviness.
normal.cn: weight 同音，但意思是重量。

normal.en: Wait and see keeps both halves: watch and hold back.
normal.cn: wait and see 保留了两面：观望与按捺。

abstract.en: See a figure at a stop, eyes on the far end of the road.
abstract.cn: 想站台上一人，眼睛盯着路的尽头。

abstract.en: Hear a clock tick while nothing moves.
abstract.cn: 听钟表滴答，什么也没动。

abstract.en: Feel the small effort of not doing anything yet.
abstract.cn: 感受暂时不动手的那点用力。

examples.en: Please wait here while I fetch the key.
examples.cn: 我去拿钥匙，请在这里等一下。

examples.en: I can hardly wait for the holidays.
examples.cn: 我简直等不及放假了。

examples.en: The queue was long, but the wait was worth it.
examples.cn: 队伍很长，但等得值得。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂特」——喂，特地在这儿站着等你，别让我白等。

root: 日耳曼语 *waht-（观望、守夜）→ 古法语北部方言 waitier（观望、埋伏）→ 英语 wait。

sensesIntro.en: A watching verb splits into four: standing still, holding back an act, attending on someone, and lying hidden, before becoming a stretch of time.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个「观望」动词分成四路：站着不动、按住行动、在旁伺候、藏着伺机，最后又变成一段时间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person fixed at a stop, watching the road.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人钉在站台上盯着路。

branches.en: The standing branch: an hour at the bus stop.
branches.cn: 守候分支：在车站等一小时。

branches.en: The delay branch: wait until the paint dries.
branches.cn: 推迟分支：等漆干了再说。

branches.en: The service branch: waiting at table.
branches.cn: 伺候分支：在餐桌旁伺候。

branches.en: The ambush branch: hunters hidden in reeds.
branches.cn: 埋伏分支：藏在芦苇里的猎人。

branches.en: The noun and the phrase: a long wait, and wait and see.
branches.cn: 名词与短语分支：漫长的等待，以及静观其变。

intro.en: Wait is short and English; -er, -ess and -ing do all the work of building the family.
intro.cn: wait 本身短小，词族全靠 -er、-ess、-ing 等词尾搭起来。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic, not Latin, so this entry lists no Latin word.
latinIntro.cn: 词根为日耳曼语而非拉丁语，故不列拉丁词条。

items.exampleCN: 这个动词是词族的基底。

items.exampleCN: wait for 是最常见的搭配。
