items.exampleCN: 它构成 wait on a guest。

definition_zh: 醒来；唤醒；使觉醒；醒来；守灵；航迹
definition_en: to stop sleeping, or to make someone stop sleeping
core_image: 眼睛在暗里突然睁开，窗外刚从黑变蓝
scene: 凌晨四点，窗外一声闷响，他一下子睁开了眼。She woke at four and could not fall asleep again.
sceneCN: 这里 wake 是「醒来」（第 1 个义项：从睡眠中醒过来）；句意为她四点醒来，再也睡不着。暗里突然睁眼的那一刻，就是这个词的形象。

pos.zh: 醒来；唤醒；使觉醒
守灵；守丧；航迹；尾波

collocations.phrase: wake to the sound of rain

derivatives.zh: wake 加 -en 构成，义为「唤醒；觉醒」
a- 与 wake 同源，义为「醒着的」
wake 加 -ful 构成，义为「睡不着的；警醒的」
复合词，义为「叫醒；叫醒服务」

senses.title: To stop sleeping
senses.definition: to come out of sleep by oneself
senses.definitionCN: 自己从睡眠中醒过来
senses.example: She woke at four and could not fall asleep again.
senses.exampleCN: 她四点醒来，再也睡不着。
senses.why: Old English wacan meant to come out of sleep, and the word has kept that simple picture for a thousand years.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 wacan 意为从睡中出来，这个词把这个简单的画面保留了一千年。

senses.title: To make someone stop sleeping
senses.definition: to rouse another person from sleep
senses.definitionCN: 把别人从睡眠中叫起来
senses.example: The noise of the lorry woke the whole street.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车的声音把整条街的人都吵醒了。
senses.why: English pairs wacan, to wake oneself, with weccan, to wake another; the two verbs merged into one.
senses.whyCN: 英语本有 wacan（自己醒）与 weccan（使别人醒）两个动词，后来合为一个。

senses.title: To become aware
senses.definition: to become conscious of something that was unnoticed
senses.definitionCN: 意识到原先未注意到的事
senses.example: The town woke to the danger only after the river rose.
senses.exampleCN: 直到河水上涨，全镇才意识到危险。
senses.why: Leaving sleep and coming to awareness are the same movement of the mind, so the word covers both.
senses.whyCN: 离开睡眠与明白过来是心智的同一种动向，这个词于是两义兼具。

senses.title: A watch over the dead
senses.definition: a gathering beside a body before burial, or a vigil
senses.definitionCN: 下葬前守在遗体旁的相聚，或守夜
senses.example: Neighbours kept a wake in the old house all night.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居们在那座老屋里守了一整夜灵。
senses.why: A wake was originally a night watch, and watching through the night gave the ceremony its name.
senses.whyCN: wake 原本是一次夜间守望，通夜守看的做法把名字给了这场仪式。

senses.title: The track left in water
senses.definition: the trail of disturbed water left behind a moving ship
senses.definitionCN: 船行进后在身后留下的水痕
senses.example: A small boat bobbed in the wake of the ferry.
senses.exampleCN: 小船在渡轮的尾波里上下摇晃。
senses.why: The track behind a ship shows where it has passed, and that visible track became the phrase in the wake of.
senses.whyCN: 船后的水痕标出它经过之处，这道看得见的痕迹便成了短语 in the wake of。

senses.title: A yearly village holiday
senses.definition: in the north of England, an annual local holiday once held at a church dedication
senses.definitionCN: 英格兰北部一年一度的村镇节日，原与教堂献堂日相连
senses.example: The whole village closes for the wake in August.
senses.exampleCN: 八月年节时整个村子都歇业。
senses.why: The night watch before a feast grew into the feast itself, so a village holiday still carries the name.
senses.whyCN: 节日前的守夜发展成了节日本身，于是村镇假日仍沿用这个名字。

intro.en: Wake is an Old English strong verb, and the noun for a night watch comes from the same root.
intro.cn: wake 是古英语的强变化动词，名词「守夜」同出这一词根。

items.en: Wacan meant to come out of sleep, and weccan meant to rouse another.
items.cn: wacan 意为从睡中出来，weccan 意为叫醒别人。

items.en: Related forms in other Germanic tongues all mean to be awake or to watch.
items.cn: 其他日耳曼语中的相关形式都表示醒着或守夜。

items.en: In Middle English the two verbs merged, and woke replaced the older past form.
items.cn: 中古英语里两个动词合并，woke 取代了较早的过去式。

items.en: The noun for a night watch over the dead became the funeral wake.
items.cn: 表示夜间守候的名词发展为守灵仪式。

items.en: Sailors used wake for the water track behind a ship, and the phrase in the wake of followed.
items.cn: 水手用 wake 指船后水痕，短语 in the wake of 随之出现。

note.en: The first group holds the words built on the same root, the second the words for sleep and waking nearby.
note.cn: 第一组收同一词根上的词，第二组收周围与睡醒相关的词。

entries.definition: The usual past tense of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词常用过去式。

entries.definition: The past participle, as in has woken.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词，如 has woken。

entries.definition: A more formal verb meaning to wake or to be woken.
entries.definitionCN: 更正式的动词，义为唤醒或醒来。

entries.definition: An adjective for not being asleep, from the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为醒着的，同出此根。

entries.definition: To get out of bed, the step after waking.
entries.definitionCN: 起床，是醒来之后的动作。

entries.definition: To wake someone, often with effort.
entries.definitionCN: 叫醒某人，常需费力。

entries.definition: A literary verb for waking or being woken.
entries.definitionCN: 文学色彩较浓，义为唤醒、醒来。

entries.definition: The state that waking ends.
entries.definitionCN: 醒来所结束的状态。

normalIntro.en: One short strong verb, three irregular forms, and a noun that means two very different things.
normalIntro.cn: 一个短小的强变化动词、三个不规则形式，再加上一个指两种不同事物的名词。

normal.en: Wake, woke, woken: a strong verb that changes its vowel.
normal.cn: wake、woke、woken：改变元音的强变化动词。

normal.en: Waken and awaken are more formal and more often transitive.
normal.cn: waken 与 awaken 更正式，更多用作及物动词。

normal.en: Wake up is the everyday phrase; up adds no new meaning.
normal.cn: wake up 是日常说法，up 不添新义。

normal.en: In the wake of means following after a ship or after an event.
normal.cn: in the wake of 指跟着船或跟着事件而来。

normal.en: A funeral wake is a watch through the night.
normal.cn: 守灵就是在夜里守着。

abstract.en: See eyelids open while the room is still dark.
abstract.cn: 想房间还暗着，眼皮忽然睁开。

abstract.en: Hear a horn outside split the silence of the morning.
abstract.cn: 听外头号声划破清晨的安静。

abstract.en: Picture a white trail widening behind a ferry.
abstract.cn: 想渡轮身后那条渐渐变宽的白痕。

examples.en: I usually wake before the alarm.
examples.cn: 我通常比闹钟先醒。

examples.en: Please wake me at six.
examples.cn: 请六点叫醒我。

examples.en: The storm left broken roofs in its wake.
examples.cn: 风暴过后留下一片破屋顶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维克」——维克在凌晨被闹钟叫醒，睁眼第一件事是关它。

root: 古英语 wacan（醒来）与 weccan（唤醒），同出日耳曼语词根；名词 wake（守夜、航迹）同源。

sensesIntro.en: For a thousand years the word has meant leaving sleep, and the night watch of the same root keeps to itself in a dark corner.
sensesIntro.cn: 一千年来这个词都指「离开睡眠」，同根的夜间守望则独自待在另一个昏暗角落。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: eyes opening in the dark.
core.cn: 核心意象：暗里睁开的眼。

branches.en: The waking branch: waking at four by oneself.
branches.cn: 醒来分支：四点自己醒来。

branches.en: The rousing branch: a lorry waking the street.
branches.cn: 唤醒分支：卡车吵醒整条街。

branches.en: The awareness branch: a town waking to danger.
branches.cn: 觉醒分支：全镇意识到危险。

branches.en: The vigil branch: a wake for the dead, then a village feast.
branches.cn: 守夜分支：守灵，进而成为村镇节庆。

branches.en: The water branch: a boat bobbing behind a ferry.
branches.cn: 水痕分支：渡轮后摇荡的小船。

intro.en: Wake is short; -en, -ful, -ing, -s and the a- and up particles extend it.
intro.cn: wake 很短，靠 -en、-ful、-ing、-s 以及 a-、up 等成分扩展。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic and has no Latin source, so this entry lists no Latin word.
latinIntro.cn: 词根为日耳曼语，没有拉丁语来源，故不列拉丁词条。

items.example: The root carries the state of waking.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根携带「醒」的状态。

items.example: The short form is the base.
It forms in the wake of.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 in the wake of。
sleep 是醒来所结束的事。

definition_zh: 唤醒；使醒来；醒来；觉醒
definition_en: to wake, or to make someone wake, especially in a formal or literary way
core_image: 一只手轻轻碰肩，睡着的人慢慢睁开眼睛
scene: 清晨的营地里，领队沿着帐篷一个个走过，轻声把大家叫起来。He was wakened by the sound of the gate opening.
sceneCN: 这里 waken 是「被唤醒」（第 1 个义项：使从睡眠中醒来）；句意为大门开动的声音把他弄醒了。有人轻碰肩膀、睡者慢慢睁眼，正是这个词的形象。

pos.zh: 唤醒；使醒来；醒来；觉醒

derivatives.zh: 去掉后缀 -en 得到的短形，义为「醒来；唤醒」
a- 与 wake 同源，义为「醒着的」
加 -ing 构成，义为「觉醒；唤醒」

senses.title: To make someone wake
senses.definition: to cause a sleeping person to wake, often by sound or touch
senses.definitionCN: 通过声音或触碰使睡着的人醒来
senses.example: He was wakened by the sound of the gate opening.
senses.exampleCN: 大门开启的声音把他弄醒了。
senses.why: Old English had weccan for waking another; adding -en made a regular verb from the same idea, still slightly formal today.
senses.whyCN: 古英语本有 weccan 表示叫醒别人，加上 -en 从同一想法造出规则动词，至今仍略偏正式。

senses.title: To wake oneself
senses.definition: to come out of sleep, used without an object
senses.definitionCN: 不带宾语时表示自己从睡中醒来
senses.example: She wakened before the light and listened to the birds.
senses.exampleCN: 天亮前她醒来，听着鸟叫。
senses.why: The suffixed verb works both ways, so the same form turns to the sleeper as subject.
senses.whyCN: 带后缀的动词两边都通，同一形式也可以让睡者作主语。

senses.title: To stir a feeling or a memory
senses.definition: to bring a feeling or a memory back into active thought
senses.definitionCN: 使某种感情或记忆重新回到意识中
senses.example: The old song wakened memories of the village.
senses.exampleCN: 那首老歌唤起了对村庄的记忆。
senses.why: Waking a person and waking a memory are the same act of setting something asleep into motion.
senses.whyCN: 把人叫醒与把记忆叫醒是同一个动作：让睡着的东西重新动起来。

senses.title: To come to awareness
senses.definition: to become aware of a situation, especially something wrong
senses.definitionCN: 意识到某种状况，尤其是不对劲的状况
senses.example: The village was wakened to the danger of the river.
senses.exampleCN: 全村终于意识到这条河的危险。
senses.why: The formal verb suits public statements, so it carries the sense of slow collective awareness better than wake.
senses.whyCN: 正式动词适合公共表述，因此比 wake 更能表达缓慢的集体觉醒。

senses.title: To rouse activity
senses.definition: to cause something dormant to become active again
senses.definitionCN: 使沉寂之物重新活跃起来
senses.example: The new market wakened trade in the small town.
senses.exampleCN: 新市场让这座小镇的贸易活了起来。
senses.why: From people the verb reaches anything that can sleep or stir, such as trade, interest or a quiet street.
senses.whyCN: 从人可以推到任何能「睡着」或「动弹」的事物，如贸易、兴趣或安静的街道。

intro.en: Waken is wake plus the old verb ending -en, which makes a verb from a verb without changing the meaning.
intro.cn: waken 是 wake 加古动词词尾 -en，由动词造出动词，而意义不变。

items.en: Wacan meant to wake and weccan meant to wake another.
items.cn: wacan 意为醒来，weccan 意为叫醒别人。

items.en: The -en ending was added in the Middle English period to make a regular form.
items.cn: 中古英语时期加上 -en 词尾，构成规则形式。

items.en: The new verb avoided the awkward past wook and spread quickly in writing.
items.cn: 新动词避开了别扭的过去式 wook，很快在书面语中流行。

items.en: Later English preferred wake with up for speech and waken for formal prose.
items.cn: 此后英语口语多用 wake up，正式散文多用 waken。

items.en: The figurative senses of memory and awareness came with the formal register.
items.cn: 记忆与觉悟的比喻义随正式语体一并出现。

note.en: The first group holds the wake family, the second the near synonyms with their differences.
note.cn: 第一组收 wake 词族，第二组收近义词及彼此的差别。

entries.definition: The third person singular form.
entries.definitionCN: 第三人称单数形式。

entries.definition: The past tense and past participle.
entries.definitionCN: 过去式与过去分词。

entries.definition: The shorter everyday verb, with woke and woken.
entries.definitionCN: 更短的日常动词，过去式与过去分词为 woke、woken。

entries.definition: A near twin, slightly more literary.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎同义，更具文学色彩。

entries.definition: To wake someone, often with effort or by shaking.
entries.definitionCN: 费力地叫醒，常伴推摇。

entries.definition: Chiefly to stir a feeling or a reaction.
entries.definitionCN: 主要表示激起感情或反应。

entries.definition: To move lightly or to begin to feel something.
entries.definitionCN: 轻轻动一下，或开始有某种感受。

entries.definition: To warn someone so that they are ready.
entries.definitionCN: 提醒某人使其准备好。

normalIntro.en: Add -en to a short verb and it becomes formal: waken, broaden, deepen.
normalIntro.cn: 给短动词加 -en 会变得正式：waken、broaden、deepen 都是如此。

normal.en: Waken is regular: waken, wakened, wakened.
normal.cn: waken 是规则动词：waken、wakened、wakened。

normal.en: Awaken and waken are near twins; awaken is more literary.
normal.cn: awaken 与 waken 近似孪生，awaken 更具文学味。

normal.en: Waken can take an object or stand alone.
normal.cn: waken 既可带宾语，也可单独使用。

normal.en: The -en ending also appears in broaden and deepen.
normal.cn: -en 词尾也见于 broaden、deepen。

normal.en: Waken interest and waken memories use the same stirring idea.
normal.cn: waken interest 与 waken memories 用的是同一种「唤起」。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on a shoulder early in the morning.
abstract.cn: 想清晨一只手轻轻落在肩上。

abstract.en: Hear a gate swing open and a sleeper sit up.
abstract.cn: 听大门开动，睡着的人坐了起来。

abstract.en: Feel an old song bringing a whole village back.
abstract.cn: 感受一首老歌把整个村庄带回来。

examples.en: The birds wakened him long before sunrise.
examples.cn: 日出之前很久，鸟叫声就把他弄醒了。

examples.en: She wakened slowly, unsure of the room.
examples.cn: 她慢慢醒来，一时认不清这间屋子。

examples.en: The letter wakened old fears.
examples.cn: 这封信唤起了旧日的恐惧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂肯」——喂，肯，快肯睁眼，天亮该起了。

root: wake（古英语 wacan / weccan，醒来、唤醒）+ 古动词词尾 -en → waken；同族词有 awaken、wakeful。

sensesIntro.en: One suffixed verb stretches from a shoulder touched in the dark to a village waking to danger.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个带后缀的动词从暗里被碰到的肩膀，一直伸到意识到危险的全村。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand on a shoulder and slowly opening eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：手落在肩上，眼睛慢慢睁开。

branches.en: The rousing branch: wakened by a gate.
branches.cn: 唤醒分支：被大门声弄醒。

branches.en: The self-waking branch: waking before the light.
branches.cn: 自醒分支：天亮前醒来。

branches.en: The memory branch: an old song waking memories.
branches.cn: 记忆分支：老歌唤起回忆。

branches.en: The awareness branch: a village waking to a river's danger.
branches.cn: 觉悟分支：全村意识到河流的危险。

branches.en: The activity branch: a market waking trade.
branches.cn: 活跃分支：市场让贸易活起来。

intro.en: Wak- is the wake root and -en is the old verb-making ending; the rest is plain English.
intro.cn: wak- 是 wake 词根，-en 是古老的造动词词尾，其余都是普通英语变化。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic; no Latin form belongs to it, so the entry lists none.
latinIntro.cn: 词根为日耳曼语，没有对应的拉丁形式，故不列拉丁词条。

items.example: The root carries the waking act.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根携带「醒」的动作。

items.example: One can waken an interest again.

definition_zh: 漫游；闲逛；迷路；走神；（道路、河流）蜿蜒
definition_en: to walk slowly with no fixed direction or aim, or to drift away from the subject
core_image: 一个人在陌生的小巷里左拐右转，没有目的地
scene: 下午的旧城里，游客不查地图，随便顺着石阶往上走。We wandered through the old quarter until the light began to fail.
sceneCN: 这里 wander 是「闲逛、漫游」（第 1 个义项：没有固定方向地慢慢走）；句意为我们在老城区闲逛，直到天色暗下来。顺着石阶随便走的那副样子，就是这个词的形象。

pos.zh: 漫游；闲逛；迷路；走神；（路、河）蜿蜒
闲逛；漫步

collocations.phrase: a river wanders through the fields

derivatives.zh: wander 加 -er 构成，义为「漫游者；流浪者」
加 -ing 构成，义为「漫游的；流浪的」
复数形式，义为「漫游；游历见闻」
同族动词，义为「行走；往…去」，常见于 wend one's way

senses.title: To move about without a fixed course
senses.definition: to move from place to place without a planned route or a clear aim
senses.definitionCN: 无预定路线、无明确目的地地四处走动
senses.example: We wandered through the old quarter until the light began to fail.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在老城区闲逛，直到天色暗下来。
senses.why: Old English wandrian meant to move about with no fixed purpose, and the core of the word has never changed.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 wandrian 指漫无目的地四处移动，这个词的核心至今未变。

senses.title: To stray from the way
senses.definition: to leave the proper path or the group, sometimes getting lost
senses.definitionCN: 离开该走的路或队伍，有时会迷路
senses.example: One child wandered off near the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 一个孩子在桥边走散了。
senses.why: Without a course, the next step is to lose the course; straying is a natural extension of aimless movement.
senses.whyCN: 没有路线，下一步便是丢了路线；走散是漫无目的移动的自然延伸。

senses.title: Of the mind, to drift
senses.definition: of thoughts, to drift from one topic to another without control
senses.definitionCN: 指思绪不受控制地从一个题目飘到另一个
senses.example: His mind began to wander as the lecture went on.
senses.exampleCN: 讲座继续时他的心思开始游移。
senses.why: Thoughts move the way feet do when no goal holds them, so the same verb covers both.
senses.whyCN: 没有目标约束时，思绪移动的方式正如脚步，于是同一个动词兼指二者。

senses.title: To diverge from the point
senses.definition: to talk or write in a way that leaves the main subject
senses.definitionCN: 说话或写作时离开主要话题
senses.example: The speaker wandered from the question more than once.
senses.exampleCN: 发言者不止一次偏离了问题。
senses.why: Wandering from a road and wandering from a subject are the same picture: off the marked line.
senses.whyCN: 从路上走开与从话题上走开是同一幅图：离开了标好的线。

senses.title: Of a road or a river, to curve
senses.definition: to extend in a winding course rather than a straight line
senses.definitionCN: 以弯曲而非直线的路径延伸
senses.example: A narrow path wanders along the bank.
senses.exampleCN: 一条小径沿河岸蜿蜒。
senses.why: A road with no straight aim goes round and round, which is exactly the movement of a wanderer.
senses.whyCN: 不取直线目标的道路绕来绕去，正与漫游者的走法相同。

senses.title: A walk taken without aim
senses.definition: in informal use, a slow walk with no purpose
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指没有目的的缓慢行走
senses.example: We went for a wander along the seafront.
senses.exampleCN: 我们沿着海滨随便走了走。
senses.why: The noun simply packages the verb's aimless walk as an outing.
senses.whyCN: 名词把动词那个无目的的走法打包成一次外出。

intro.en: Wander is an Old English verb of uncertain deeper origin, already meaning to roam.
intro.cn: wander 是古英语动词，更早来源不确定，当时已表示漫游。

items.en: Wandrian meant to move about without a fixed purpose; it already had the modern sense.
items.cn: wandrian 意为无固定目的地四处移动，已具现代含义。

items.en: A related Germanic verb wanden meant to go or to wend, and gave English wend.
items.cn: 相关的日耳曼语动词 wanden 意为去、行走，生出英语 wend。

items.en: The deeper root is debated; some link it to a word for twisting, but nothing is settled.
items.cn: 更早词根有争议，有人认为与表示「扭、绕」的词有关，但无定论。

items.en: English kept the plain sense of roaming and added the mind's drifting in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语保留漫游的基本义，十六世纪又添上思绪游移之义。

items.en: Modern use adds the winding of paths and rivers and the informal noun.
items.cn: 现代用法又添上路径与河流的蜿蜒，以及口语名词。

note.en: The first group holds the words of the same root and spelling neighbours, the second the walking words it is confused with.
note.cn: 第一组收同根词与拼写相近词，第二组收容易混淆的行走类词。

entries.definition: A person who wanders; a rover.
entries.definitionCN: 漫游者、流浪者。

entries.definition: The act of roaming, or an adjective for it.
entries.definitionCN: 漫游，也可作形容词。

entries.definition: A different word meaning amazement or to ask oneself.
entries.definitionCN: 另一个词，义为惊奇、想知道。

entries.definition: A related verb in wend one's way, meaning to go.
entries.definitionCN: 相关动词，见于 wend one's way，义为行走。

entries.definition: To travel widely over a large area, often with ease.
entries.definitionCN: 在广大区域里自在游走。

entries.definition: To walk slowly and pleasantly, usually with company.
entries.definitionCN: 悠闲地、常与人同行地慢慢走。

entries.definition: To get lost or move off the proper place.
entries.definitionCN: 走失、离开应处之地。

entries.definition: To be carried along without control, often of the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 不受控制地被带走，常用于思绪。

normalIntro.en: Footsteps with no course, then a mind with no course, then a path with no straight line.
normalIntro.cn: 没有路线的脚步，接着是没有路线的思绪，最后是没有直线的路径。

normal.en: Wander and wonder differ by one letter: roam versus ask oneself.
normal.cn: wander 与 wonder 只差一个字母：漫游与想知道。

normal.en: Wander is regular: wander, wandered, wandered.
normal.cn: wander 是规则动词：wander、wandered、wandered。

normal.en: Wander off means stray away; wander from means leave the subject.
normal.cn: wander off 是走散，wander from 是偏离话题。

normal.en: A wanderer wanders; his wanderings fill a book.
normal.cn: a wanderer 漫游，他的 wanderings 可以写成书。

normal.en: Wend one's way shares the old root of wander.
normal.cn: wend one's way 与 wander 同出旧词根。

abstract.en: See feet turning left, then right, along lanes.
abstract.cn: 想象双脚在小巷里左拐右拐。

abstract.en: Hear a voice trail off into an unrelated story.
abstract.cn: 听一个声音慢慢拐进不相干的故事。

abstract.en: Picture a path drawing a long loop along a river bank.
abstract.cn: 想象小径沿河岸画出一个大弯。

examples.en: The children wandered in and out of the shops.
examples.cn: 孩子们在店铺之间进进出出地闲逛。

examples.en: Don't let your attention wander from the road.
examples.cn: 别让注意力离开路面。

examples.en: The stream wanders through the meadow.
examples.cn: 小溪蜿蜒穿过草甸。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弯的」——路是弯的，顺着弯弯的巷子一直走，就叫漫游。

root: 古英语 wandrian（漫游），同出日耳曼语词根（参 wend）；更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: No goal is the thread: feet roam, feet stray, thoughts drift, talk leaves the point, and roads wind.
sensesIntro.cn: 「没有目标」是这条线索：脚漫游、脚走散、思绪飘、话语离题、道路绕弯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: steps turning corners with no destination.
core.cn: 核心意象：在巷子里拐来拐去、没有目的的脚步。

branches.en: The roaming branch: an afternoon in the old quarter.
branches.cn: 漫游分支：在老城区逛一个下午。

branches.en: The straying branch: a child lost by the bridge.
branches.cn: 走散分支：桥边走散的孩子。

branches.en: The mind branch: attention slipping during a lecture.
branches.cn: 思绪分支：听讲座时注意力滑走。

branches.en: The course branch: a talk off the point, a path along a bank.
branches.cn: 路线分支：离题的谈话与沿河的小径。

branches.en: The outing branch: a wander along the seafront.
branches.cn: 外出分支：沿海滨随便走走。

intro.en: Wand- is the roaming root; -er, -ing and -s do the building.
intro.cn: wand- 是「漫游」词根，词族由 -er、-ing、-s 搭建。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic and uncertain beyond that, so no Latin word is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 词根为日耳曼语，再往上不确定，故不列拉丁词条。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根携带无目的的移动。

items.example: It forms wander from the subject.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 wander from the subject。

items.example: It forms wander around the town.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 wander around the town。

definition_zh: 衣柜；衣橱；（个人的）全部衣服；戏服部
definition_en: a tall cupboard in which clothes are hung, or the whole set of clothes a person owns
core_image: 一扇高柜门打开，里面挂满一排衣服
scene: 搬家那天，最沉的家具就是卧室里那个高柜，两个人才抬得动。She hung the coat in the wardrobe and closed the door.
sceneCN: 这里 wardrobe 是「衣柜」「衣橱」（第 1 个义项：挂衣服的高柜）；句意为她把大衣挂进衣柜，关上了门。柜门打开见到一排衣服，就是这个词的形象。

pos.zh: 衣柜；衣橱；全部衣服；戏服部

derivatives.zh: 复数形式，义为「多个衣柜；各处衣物」
该词的前半部分，义为「守护；看守」
该词的后半部分，义为「长袍」
美式常用同义词，义为「壁橱；衣橱」

senses.title: The tall cupboard for clothes
senses.definition: a tall piece of furniture with a rail, in which clothes are hung
senses.definitionCN: 带挂杆、用来挂衣服的高家具
senses.example: She hung the coat in the wardrobe and closed the door.
senses.exampleCN: 她把大衣挂进衣柜，关上了门。
senses.why: The word first named a room where clothes were kept under watch, from ward, to guard, and robe, a gown.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指有人守护、存放衣服的房间，由 ward（看守）与 robe（长袍）组成。

senses.title: The whole set of clothes owned
senses.definition: all the clothes a person has, thought of as one collection
senses.definitionCN: 一个人拥有的所有衣服，被当作一个整体
senses.example: He spent the winter building a warmer wardrobe.
senses.exampleCN: 他整个冬天都在置办更暖和的一批衣服。
senses.why: When clothes moved from a guarded room into a cupboard, the name went with them and extended to the collection itself.
senses.whyCN: 衣服从有人看守的房间搬进柜子后，名字跟着走，并扩展到整批衣服。

senses.title: The stock of costumes for a company
senses.definition: the supply of costumes kept by a theatre or a film company
senses.definitionCN: 剧团或电影公司存有的演出服装
senses.example: The wardrobe was rebuilt for the new production.
senses.exampleCN: 为新剧目重新置办了戏服。
senses.why: A theatre needs a guarded store of costumes as a household needs one for clothes, so the same word serves both.
senses.whyCN: 剧团需要有人管理的戏服库，正如家庭需要存衣之处，同一个词两边都用。

senses.title: A collection of available styles
senses.definition: in figurative use, the range of styles or approaches a person can draw on
senses.definitionCN: 比喻中指一个人可以调用的风格或手段
senses.example: The writer has a wide wardrobe of voices.
senses.exampleCN: 这位作家有多种可供调用的写作声音。
senses.why: If clothes can be a collection one picks from, so can styles, tricks and methods.
senses.whyCN: 既然衣服是可以挑选的一批，风格、招数与手法也可以。

senses.title: A form of royal household office
senses.definition: in older use, the office or the room in a palace that kept the royal robes
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法，指宫中保管御衣的职位或房间
senses.example: A clerk of the wardrobe kept a record of the king's robes.
senses.exampleCN: 掌衣房的书记记录国王的袍服。
senses.why: A royal household could not leave its costly robes unwatched, so a whole department grew around this word.
senses.whyCN: 王室不能把贵重袍服放着无人看守，于是围绕这个词长出整个机构。

intro.en: Wardrobe joins two Old French words: ward, a guard, and robe, a gown.
intro.cn: wardrobe 由两个古法语词合成：ward（看守）与 robe（长袍）。

items.en: Ward came from a Germanic root meaning to watch or to guard.
items.cn: ward 来自日耳曼语表示观望、守护的词根。

items.en: Old French garderobe named a room where clothes and valuables were kept under guard.
items.cn: 古法语 garderobe 指有人看守、存放衣物与贵重物品的房间。

items.en: English borrowed it in the middle ages and dropped the g of the first part.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪借入该词，并去掉了前半的 g。

items.en: As clothes moved into furniture, the word shifted from the room to the cupboard.
items.cn: 随着衣物转入家具，这个词从房间转到柜子。

items.en: Theatres and fashion then used it for a whole stock of clothes or costumes.
items.cn: 剧场与时尚界随后用它指整批衣物或戏服。

note.en: The first group holds the two halves and the near synonyms, the second the furniture and clothing words around it.
note.cn: 第一组收两个组成部分与近义词，第二组收周围家具与服装类词。

entries.definition: The plural form of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词复数。

entries.definition: The first half, meaning a guard or a hospital room.
entries.definitionCN: 前半部分，义为守护、病房。

entries.definition: The second half, meaning a long loose gown.
entries.definitionCN: 后半部分，义为长袍。

entries.definition: A person who guards, from the same root as ward.
entries.definitionCN: 与 ward 同根，指看守人。

entries.definition: The American word for a built-in clothes cupboard.
entries.definitionCN: 美式用词，指嵌入式衣橱。

entries.definition: A general storage cabinet, usually with shelves.
entries.definitionCN: 带搁板的通用储物柜。

entries.definition: A low box with a lid for folded clothes.
entries.definitionCN: 装叠好衣物的矮箱柜。

entries.definition: Clothing worn for a part or an occasion.
entries.definitionCN: 演出或特定场合穿的服装。

normalIntro.en: Guard plus gown: a watched place for robes, now a tall cupboard of hanging clothes.
normalIntro.cn: 看守加长袍：原是看守袍服之处，今天是挂着衣服的高柜。

normal.en: Wardrobe is ward (guard) plus robe (gown), with a silent final e.
normal.cn: wardrobe 是 ward（看守）加 robe（长袍），结尾 e 不发音。

normal.en: The plural is wardrobes, with no change to the stem.
normal.cn: 复数是 wardrobes，词干不变。

normal.en: A wardrobe hangs clothes; a chest stores them folded.
normal.cn: wardrobe 挂衣服，chest 放叠好的衣服。

normal.en: Your wardrobe also means all the clothes you own.
normal.cn: your wardrobe 也指你拥有的全部衣服。

normal.en: A theatre wardrobe is its stock of costumes.
normal.cn: 剧团的 wardrobe 是它的戏服库。

abstract.en: See a tall door swing open on a rail of coats.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇高门打开，露出一排挂着的外套。

abstract.en: Hear a coat hanger click along the rail.
abstract.cn: 听衣架在挂杆上滑动的轻响。

abstract.en: Picture a guarded room in an old palace full of robes.
abstract.cn: 想象老宫殿里一间有人看守、挂满袍服的房间。

examples.en: There is no space left in the wardrobe.
examples.cn: 衣柜里已经没有空位了。

examples.en: She packed half her wardrobe into one case.
examples.cn: 她把一半的衣服塞进了一个箱子。

examples.en: The coat should be kept on a hanger in a wardrobe.
examples.cn: 这件大衣应挂在衣柜里的衣架上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我追不」——衣服太多，我追不着，全塞进衣柜里。

root: 古法语 garder（看守，源自日耳曼语）+ robe（长袍）→ garderobe（看守衣物的房间）→ 英语 wardrobe（衣柜）。

sensesIntro.en: A guarded room loses its walls and becomes a cupboard, and the name then spreads to the clothes, the costumes and a collection of styles.
sensesIntro.cn: 一间有人看守的房间卸掉墙壁变成柜子，名字又顺势扩展到衣服、戏服与一批风格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tall door opening on hanging clothes.
core.cn: 核心意象：高柜门打开，一排衣服挂着。

branches.en: The furniture branch: a coat hung inside and the door closed.
branches.cn: 家具分支：大衣挂进去、门关上。

branches.en: The collection branch: a warmer set of clothes for winter.
branches.cn: 集合分支：为冬天置办的暖衣。

branches.en: The theatre branch: costumes rebuilt for a new play.
branches.cn: 剧场分支：为新戏重置的戏服。

branches.en: The metaphor branch: a writer with many voices.
branches.cn: 比喻分支：有多种笔调的作家。

branches.en: The palace branch: a clerk of the royal wardrobe.
branches.cn: 宫廷分支：掌管御衣房的书记。

intro.en: Wardrobe is a true compound of ward and robe; English only adds a plural -s.
intro.cn: wardrobe 是 ward 与 robe 的真正复合词，英语只再加复数 -s。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are Germanic in origin but entered English through Old French, and neither is a classical Latin word.
latinIntro.cn: 两半本为日耳曼语，均经古法语进入英语，都不是古典拉丁语词。

items.exampleCN: 前半部分携带「看守」之义。

items.example: The second half names the garment.

items.exampleCN: warden 与 wardrobe 共享 ward。

items.example: Guard and ward are old cousins.
items.exampleCN: guard 与 ward 是古老的同源词。

items.example: A wardrobe has a rail and shelves.

definition_zh: 温暖；暖和；热情；热心；（色彩）暖调
definition_en: the state of being warm, or the friendly feeling shown to others
core_image: 两只手握着一杯热茶，热气慢慢升上来
scene: 雪后的屋子里，炉火刚点起来，玻璃上蒙了一层白雾。We stood by the stove and felt the warmth come back into our hands.
sceneCN: 这里 warmth 是「温暖」（第 1 个义项：暖和的状态）；句意为我们站在炉边，感到手渐渐回暖。握杯热茶时那股慢慢升起来的热，就是这个词的形象。

pos.zh: 温暖；暖和；热情；热心；暖调

derivatives.zh: 去掉后缀 -th 得到的形容词，义为「暖的；热情的」
warm 加 -ly 构成，义为「温暖地；热情地」
加 -less 构成，义为「无暖意的」
复合词，义为「热身」

senses.title: The state of being warm
senses.definition: a moderate degree of heat, comfortable rather than hot
senses.definitionCN: 适中、令人舒适而不烫的热度
senses.example: We stood by the stove and felt the warmth come back into our hands.
senses.exampleCN: 我们站在炉边，感到手渐渐回暖。
senses.why: Warm is the adjective, and -th turns it into the noun for the state itself, as true turns to truth.
senses.whyCN: warm 是形容词，-th 把它变成表示状态本身的名词，正如 true 变 truth。

senses.title: Friendly feeling shown
senses.definition: kindness and friendliness in manner, which people feel as comfort
senses.definitionCN: 举止中的善意与亲切，让人感到舒适
senses.example: The warmth of the welcome surprised the visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 主人的热情让来访者十分意外。
senses.why: Bodily heat is a comfort, and a friendly manner gives the same comfort, so the word carries over without effort.
senses.whyCN: 身上的暖是舒适，亲切的态度也给出同样的舒适，于是词义自然沿用。

senses.title: Heat in a place or an object
senses.definition: the heat stored in something, as felt by touch
senses.definitionCN: 物体存有的热，可凭触觉感到
senses.example: The warmth of the stone bench stayed after sunset.
senses.exampleCN: 石凳上的热在日落后仍未散。
senses.why: A stone keeps the heat it has taken, and the word for the state simply stays with the object.
senses.whyCN: 石头会留住它所吸收的热，表示这种状态的名词便留在了物体上。

senses.title: The warm quality of a colour
senses.definition: the effect of colours such as red and yellow, which seem to give off heat
senses.definitionCN: 红黄一类颜色给人的、仿佛散发热量的感觉
senses.example: The painter added warmth to the grey street with a few red roofs.
senses.exampleCN: 画家用几片红屋顶给灰冷的街道添了暖调。
senses.why: Reds and yellows recall fire and sun, so painters describe them with the same word for heat.
senses.whyCN: 红与黄让人想到火与太阳，画家于是用表示热的同一个词来描述它们。

senses.title: Heat in a voice or a sound
senses.definition: a quality in a voice that sounds kind, full and alive
senses.definitionCN: 声音中显得亲切、饱满而有生气的特质
senses.example: There was warmth in her voice that the letter could not carry.
senses.exampleCN: 她声音里的暖意是信里带不出来的。
senses.why: A kind voice gives the listener the same comfort as heat gives the skin, so the word covers both.
senses.whyCN: 和善的声音给听者的舒适，正如热给皮肤的舒适，这个词便两处都用。

intro.en: Warmth is warm plus the old noun ending -th, which turns an adjective into a state.
intro.cn: warmth 是 warm 加古老的名词词尾 -th，把形容词变成状态名词。

items.en: The adjective had a root meaning warm in Old English, with a related noun for heat.
items.cn: 这个形容词的古英语形式本有「暖」的含义，并有表示热的相关名词。

items.en: Related forms in other Germanic tongues all mean warm.
items.cn: 其他日耳曼语中的相关形式都表示「暖」。

items.en: The noun warmth settled in the Middle English period beside older forms now lost.
items.cn: 名词 warmth 在中古英语时期定型，与已废弃的更旧形式并存。

items.en: The -th ending is the same one in truth, length and depth.
items.cn: -th 词尾与 truth、length、depth 中的相同。

items.en: The sense of friendship and the sense of colour warmth both developed in modern usage.
items.cn: 友谊义与色彩暖调义都在现代用法中形成。

note.en: The first group holds the words of the same family, the second the other words for heat and kindness.
note.cn: 第一组收同族词，第二组收表示热与亲切的其他词。

entries.definition: The adjective, meaning moderately hot or friendly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「温暖的、热情的」。

entries.definition: The adverb, meaning in a friendly or heated way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「温暖地、热情地」。

entries.definition: A rare adjective for having no warmth.
entries.definitionCN: 罕见形容词，义为「无暖意的」。

entries.definition: Exercise or preparation done before the main activity.
entries.definitionCN: 主活动前的热身或准备。

entries.definition: High temperature, often uncomfortable.
entries.definitionCN: 高温，常令人不适。

entries.definition: The quality of being caring and helpful.
entries.definitionCN: 关心体贴的品质。

entries.definition: A fond feeling toward someone.
entries.definitionCN: 对某人的喜爱之情。

entries.definition: Ease of body or mind, often what warmth gives.
entries.definitionCN: 身心的舒适，常由温暖带来。

normalIntro.en: Add -th to an adjective and it becomes a state: warm, length, depth, truth.
normalIntro.cn: 给形容词加 -th 就成状态名词：warm、length、depth、truth 都是这条路。

normal.en: Warmth is warm plus -th, like true to truth.
normal.cn: warmth 是 warm 加 -th，正如 true 变 truth。

normal.en: Warmth is uncountable: some warmth, not a warmth.
normal.cn: warmth 不可数：说 some warmth，不说 a warmth。

normal.en: Heat is too strong; warmth is the comfortable middle.
normal.cn: heat 太强，warmth 是舒适的那一档。

normal.en: Warmth of feeling is friendliness you can almost feel on the skin.
normal.cn: 情感的 warmth 是几乎能用皮肤感到的亲切。

normal.en: Warmth of colour means reds and yellows, not blues.
normal.cn: warmth of colour 指红黄，而不是蓝。

abstract.en: See two hands around a hot cup and steam rising.
abstract.cn: 想象两手持杯、热气上升。

abstract.en: Feel a stove begin to give out heat into a cold room.
abstract.cn: 感受炉子开始向冷屋子放热。

abstract.en: Hear a greeting said gently, without hurry.
abstract.cn: 听一声不急不忙、温和的问候。

examples.en: The warmth of the fire reached the far wall.
examples.cn: 炉火的热一直传到了远墙。

examples.en: She greeted the guests with great warmth.
examples.cn: 她非常热情地迎接客人。

examples.en: The blanket kept the warmth in all night.
examples.cn: 毯子整夜把暖意留住。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「窝木室」——窝在木屋里烤火，满室都是暖意。

root: 古英语形容词「暖」（同出日耳曼语）+ 名词词尾 -th → warmth；同型词有 length、depth、truth。

sensesIntro.en: One state spreads from a stove to a welcome, to stone that keeps heat, to red roofs, to a voice.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一种状态从炉子传到欢迎、传到存热的石头、传到红屋顶、再传到一副嗓音里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands around a hot cup.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手握着一杯热茶。

branches.en: The comfort branch: hands warming at a stove.
branches.cn: 舒适分支：在炉边烘暖的手。

branches.en: The friendship branch: a welcome that surprised guests.
branches.cn: 情谊分支：让客人意外的欢迎。

branches.en: The stored-heat branch: a stone bench after sunset.
branches.cn: 蓄热分支：日落后仍温的石凳。

branches.en: The colour branch: red roofs on a grey street.
branches.cn: 色彩分支：灰街上的一片红屋顶。

branches.en: The voice branch: warmth that a letter cannot carry.
branches.cn: 声音分支：信里带不出的暖意。

intro.en: Warm- is the adjective and -th makes the state noun; every other word is built on warm.
intro.cn: warm- 是形容词，-th 造出状态名词，其余词都由 warm 派生。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic, so no Latin word belongs to it; the -th ending is native English as well.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是日耳曼语，没有对应的拉丁语词，-th 词尾也是英语本族词尾。

items.example: The root carries the comfort of heat.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根携带热的舒适。

items.example: It forms the warmth of the sun.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 the warmth of the sun。

items.example: Coolness is the opposite of warmth.
items.exampleCN: coolness 是 warmth 的反面。

definition_zh: 美德；德行；优点；长处；效力；贞操
definition_en: a good quality of character, or a useful strength in a thing
core_image: 一个人把力气用在正处，站得笔直
scene: 毕业典礼上，老校长没有讲成绩，只讲了诚实与耐心这两件事。Patience was the one virtue the job truly required.
sceneCN: 这里 virtue 是「美德」（第 1 个义项：品格中的善）；句意为耐心是这份工作真正需要的一种美德。把力气用在正处、站得笔直的那个人，就是这个词的形象。

pos.zh: 美德；德行；优点；长处；效力

collocations.zh: 化不得已为美德；将就办事

derivatives.zh: virtue 加 -ous 构成，义为「有德行的；正直的」
同出拉丁词根 virtus，义为「几乎；实际上」
同根形容词，义为「实质上的；虚拟的」
同根名词，义为「精湛技艺」

senses.title: A good quality of character
senses.definition: a quality in a person that is good and worth praising, such as honesty or courage
senses.definitionCN: 个人身上值得赞许的善的品质，如诚实、勇气
senses.example: Patience was the one virtue the job truly required.
senses.exampleCN: 耐心是这份工作真正需要的一种美德。
senses.why: Latin virtus first meant manly strength and courage, and the word slowly moved from strength of body to strength of character used well.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 virtus 最初意为男子气概的力量与勇气，这个词慢慢从身体之力转到用得其所的品格之力。

senses.title: A good point in a thing
senses.definition: a useful strength or good feature in an object, a plan or a method
senses.definitionCN: 物体、方案或方法中可取的长处
senses.example: The chief virtue of the old car is that it never breaks down.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆旧车最大的优点是它从不坏。
senses.why: If a person can have good qualities, so can a plan; the word applies to anything with strengths worth naming.
senses.whyCN: 人能有好品质，方案也能，于是这个词用于任何值得称道的长处。

senses.title: Power to produce an effect
senses.definition: the power of something, such as a medicine or a herb, to act as it should
senses.definitionCN: 药物或草药等发挥应有作用的力量
senses.example: The virtue of the plant lies in its bitter root.
senses.exampleCN: 这种植物的效力在于它苦涩的根。
senses.why: Older medicine spoke of the virtue of a herb, meaning its active strength, which is strength again, now inside a plant.
senses.whyCN: 早期医学讲草药的 virtue，指它的有效之力，还是「力量」，只是转到了植物身上。

senses.title: Chastity, especially of a woman
senses.definition: in older use, chastity, chiefly spoken of a woman
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法，指贞洁，主要用来指女性
senses.example: The old play makes her virtue a matter of public talk.
senses.exampleCN: 那部老戏把她的贞洁写成众人议论的事。
senses.why: A narrow set of rules once gathered around the word, so one particular virtue became the virtue; modern use keeps it mainly historical.
senses.whyCN: 一套狭窄的规矩曾围着这个词，于是某一种美德就成了 the virtue；现代用法主要保留历史色彩。

senses.title: Strength shown in a fixed phrase
senses.definition: in the fixed phrases by virtue of and in virtue of, meaning because of or through
senses.definitionCN: 固定短语 by virtue of、in virtue of 中，意为凭借、由于
senses.example: She entered by virtue of her father's old pass.
senses.exampleCN: 她凭父亲旧日的通行证进去了。
senses.why: To act by virtue of something is to act on the strength given by it, so the old sense of power survives in this phrase.
senses.whyCN: by virtue of 某物行事，就是借它给的力量行事，旧有的「力量」义在这个短语里活了下来。

intro.en: Virtue comes from Latin virtus, strength or manliness, from vir, a man.
intro.cn: virtue 来自拉丁语 virtus（力量、男子气），源自 vir（男人）。

items.en: Vir meant a man, and virtus named the strength and courage expected of one.
items.cn: vir 意为男人，virtus 指男人应有的力量与勇气。

items.en: Cicero and others widened virtus to cover moral excellence of any kind.
items.cn: 西塞罗等人把 virtus 扩展到各种道德上的优秀。

items.en: Old French vertu carried the moral sense into English.
items.cn: 古法语 vertu 把道德义带进英语。

items.en: English added the sense of a good point in a thing and of the active power of a herb or stone.
items.cn: 英语又添上事物的长处，以及草药或石头的效力。

items.en: By virtue of keeps the older sense of power, and virtual grew beside it with a sense of what works in effect.
items.cn: by virtue of 保留了较旧的「力量」义，virtual 在旁边长出「实际起效」的意思。

note.en: The first group holds the same-root family, the second the words for goodness and for a good point.
note.cn: 第一组收同根词族，第二组收表示善与优点的词。

entries.definition: The plural of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词复数。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning having or showing moral goodness.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有德行的、正直的」。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning acting in effect, though not in name or fact.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「实际起作用的、虚拟的」。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning almost, or in practice.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「几乎、实际上」。

entries.definition: The quality of deserving praise, or a good point.
entries.definitionCN: 值得赞许之处，也指优点。

entries.definition: The general quality of being good.
entries.definitionCN: 善的总体品质。

entries.definition: The strengths of a case or a plan.
entries.definitionCN: 案件或方案的优点。

entries.definition: A bad habit or fault, the opposite of a virtue.
entries.definitionCN: 恶习，与美德相对。

normalIntro.en: A word for manly strength became a word for moral strength, then for any useful strength.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示男子之力的词，先变成道德之力，再变成任何可用的长处。

normal.en: Virtue comes from vir, a man, and virtus, the strength expected of him.
normal.cn: virtue 来自 vir（男人）与 virtus（他应有的力量）。

normal.en: By virtue of means because of, and keeps the old sense of power.
normal.cn: by virtue of 意为由于，保留着旧的「力量」义。

normal.en: Virtue is a good quality in a person; a virtue can also be a good point in a plan.
normal.cn: virtue 是人的好品质，也可指方案的长处。

normal.en: The plural is virtues; the adjective is virtuous.
normal.cn: 复数是 virtues，形容词是 virtuous。

normal.en: Vice is the opposite of virtue.
normal.cn: vice 是 virtue 的反面。

abstract.en: See a person standing straight with strength used for something good.
abstract.cn: 想象一人站得笔直，把力气用在正处。

abstract.en: Hear a teacher praising honesty instead of marks.
abstract.cn: 听老师不提分数，只夸诚实。

abstract.en: Feel the silent working power inside a bitter herb.
abstract.cn: 感受苦草根里那股无言的作用之力。

examples.en: Honesty is a virtue he never had to learn.
examples.cn: 诚实是他不必去学的一种美德。

examples.en: They chose the small hotel for the virtue of its quiet garden.
examples.cn: 他们选这家小旅馆，是因为它有安静花园这个优点。

examples.en: He was admitted by virtue of a special licence.
examples.cn: 他凭一张特别许可得以进入。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我求」——我求的是好品德，不是好分数。

root: 拉丁语 vir（男人）→ virtus（力量、勇气、美德）→ 古法语 vertu → 英语 virtue。

sensesIntro.en: Strength narrows to moral strength, then widens to a good point in a thing, to the power in a plant, and to a narrow historical sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 「力量」先缩成道德之力，再扩到事物的长处、植物的效力，以及一个狭窄的历史义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: strength held upright and used for good.
core.cn: 核心意象：站得笔直、用在正处的力量。

branches.en: The character branch: patience on the job.
branches.cn: 品格分支：工作所需的耐心。

branches.en: The good-point branch: a car that never breaks down.
branches.cn: 长处分支：从不坏的旧车。

branches.en: The power branch: a bitter root that works.
branches.cn: 效力分支：起作用的苦根。

branches.en: The historical branch: an old play about a woman's honour.
branches.cn: 历史分支：老戏里的名声。

branches.en: The phrase branch: entering by virtue of a pass.
branches.cn: 短语分支：凭通行证进入。

intro.en: Virt- comes from vir, a man; -ue arrived through French, and -ous, -ual, -ually build the family.
intro.cn: virt- 来自 vir（男人），-ue 经法语而来，-ous、-ual、-ually 撑起词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin vir and virtus are both recorded, and virtus is common in classical prose.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vir 与 virtus 均有记录，virtus 在古典散文里很常见。

items.example: The noun is the root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是词族的词根。

items.example: The noun first meant manly strength.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词最初指男子之力。

definition_zh: 病毒；病毒性疾病；（计算机）病毒；恶毒影响
definition_en: a tiny agent that lives inside cells and makes copies of itself, often causing disease
core_image: 一个带刺的小球贴在细胞门口，正准备钻进去复制自己
scene: 一月的急诊室里，孩子的体温降不下来，医生先排除了细菌。The doctor said a virus, not bacteria, was causing the fever.
sceneCN: 这里 virus 是「病毒」（第 1 个义项：寄生在细胞里、复制自身并能致病的微小因子）；句意为医生说引起发热的是病毒而非细菌。贴到细胞门口的那个带刺小球，正是这个词的形象。

pos.zh: 病毒；病毒性疾病；（电脑）病毒；恶毒影响

derivatives.zh: 由 virus 加 -al 构成，义为「病毒的； viral 式的」
vir 与 -ology 复合，义为「病毒学」
加 -ist 构成，义为「病毒学家」
同出拉丁词根，义为「剧毒的；恶毒的」

senses.title: A tiny disease agent
senses.definition: an infective agent too small to be seen under a normal microscope, multiplying only inside living cells
senses.definitionCN: 小到普通显微镜看不见，只能在活细胞内复制繁殖的感染因子
senses.example: The doctor said a virus, not bacteria, was causing the fever.
senses.exampleCN: 医生说引起发热的是病毒而非细菌。
senses.why: Latin virus meant poison or slime, and when scientists found an agent smaller than bacteria they gave it that old name.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 virus 意为毒液、黏液，科学家发现一种比细菌更小的因子时，就给它用了这个旧名。

senses.title: An illness caused by it
senses.definition: in everyday speech, a sickness thought to come from such an agent
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指由这类因子引起的病
senses.example: He has been off work for a week with a virus.
senses.exampleCN: 他因为一次病毒感染病休了一周。
senses.why: People name the illness after its cause, so a viral cold is simply called a virus.
senses.whyCN: 人们以病因称呼疾病，病毒性感冒就被直接叫作 a virus。

senses.title: A program that spreads itself
senses.definition: a hidden program that copies itself into other programs and damages them
senses.definitionCN: 能把自己复制到别的程序中、并造成破坏的隐藏程序
senses.example: The old laptop was slow because of a virus.
senses.exampleCN: 那台旧笔记本因为中了病毒而变慢。
senses.why: A computer virus spreads and multiplies like the biological one, so the borrowed name needed no change.
senses.whyCN: 电脑病毒像生物病毒一样传播、复制，借来的名字不必改动。

senses.title: A harmful influence
senses.definition: in literary use, something that corrupts a mind or a society
senses.definitionCN: 文学用法中指腐蚀人心或社会的东西
senses.example: The writer called envy a virus of the mind.
senses.exampleCN: 那位作家把嫉妒称为精神上的病毒。
senses.why: Poison spreading unseen is an old image for bad influence, which explains the literary sense.
senses.whyCN: 看不见地扩散的毒，是描述恶劣影响的旧意象，文学义由此而来。

senses.title: Poison in the old sense
senses.definition: in Latin and early English, a poisonous liquid or a foul humour
senses.definitionCN: 在拉丁语与早期英语里指毒液或有毒的体液
senses.example: Old medicine blamed a virus in the blood for the swelling.
senses.exampleCN: 早期医学把这种肿痛归咎于血液中的毒。
senses.why: Before viruses were seen, the word named any poison, and trace of that sense survives in virulent.
senses.whyCN: 在病毒被看见之前，这个词泛指任何毒，这层意思还留在 virulent 里。

intro.en: Virus is Latin for poison or slime, and science borrowed it as a technical term only in modern times.
intro.cn: virus 在拉丁语里指毒液或黏液，科学界只是在近代才把它借作术语。

items.en: Virus meant a poisonous liquid, slime or a foul discharge.
items.cn: virus 意为毒液、黏液或恶臭的分泌物。

items.en: English used it for poison in the seventeenth century, mostly in scientific writing.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪用它表示毒，主要用于科学写作。

items.en: After filters caught bacteria but not the smaller agent, virus was used for the new class.
items.cn: 过滤器能拦住细菌却拦不住更小的因子后，virus 被用来指这一新类别。

items.en: Electron microscopes made the particles visible in the nineteen thirties.
items.cn: 三十年代的电子显微镜使这些颗粒变得可见。

items.en: Computer use in the nineteen seventies and the adjective viral in the internet age added new branches.
items.cn: 七十年代的电脑用法与互联网时代的形容词 viral 又添了新枝。

note.en: The first group follows the family and the look-alike, the second the words for germs and their effects.
note.cn: 第一组收同族词与形近词，第二组收病菌及其影响类词。

entries.definition: The plural form of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词复数。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning of a virus, or spreading fast online.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「病毒的、在网上迅速传播的」。

entries.definition: The scientific study of viruses.
entries.definitionCN: 研究病毒的学科。

entries.definition: An adjective from the same Latin root meaning very poisonous or bitter.
entries.definitionCN: 同根形容词，义为「剧毒的、恶毒的」。

entries.definition: Single-celled organisms that can also cause disease, larger than viruses.
entries.definitionCN: 单细胞生物，也能致病，比病毒大。

entries.definition: An everyday word for any microbe that spreads disease.
entries.definitionCN: 日常用词，泛指致病微生物。

entries.definition: The condition caused when an agent enters the body.
entries.definitionCN: 病原进入身体后造成的状况。

entries.definition: An adjective for diseases spread from person to person.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，形容疾病在人际传播。

normalIntro.en: One Latin word for poison serves a microbe, a sickness, a program and a bad idea.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拉丁的「毒」字，同时服务微生物、一场病、一个程序与一个坏念头。

normal.en: Virus and virulent share a Latin root meaning poison.
normal.cn: virus 与 virulent 同出拉丁「毒」字词根。

normal.en: The plural is viruses; the adjective is viral.
normal.cn: 复数是 viruses，形容词是 viral。

normal.en: A virus needs a living cell; bacteria do not.
normal.cn: 病毒需要活细胞，细菌不需要。

normal.en: A computer virus copies itself into other programs, just as the biological one does.
normal.cn: 电脑病毒如生物病毒一样把自己复制进别的程序。

normal.en: Viral also means spreading fast on the internet.
normal.cn: viral 还指在网上迅速传播。

abstract.en: See a spiky ball landing on a cell wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一个带刺小球落在细胞壁上。

abstract.en: Hear a doctor say it is a virus, so an antibiotic will not help.
abstract.cn: 听医生说这是病毒，抗生素没用。

abstract.en: Picture a line of code quietly copying itself into a file.
abstract.cn: 想象一行代码悄悄把自己复制进一个文件。

examples.en: A virus cannot multiply without a living cell.
examples.cn: 病毒没有活细胞就不能繁殖。

examples.en: Most winter viruses spread through the air.
examples.cn: 多数冬季病毒通过空气传播。

examples.en: He lost all his files to a virus.
examples.cn: 一次病毒让他的文件全丢了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歪螺」——长得歪歪扭扭的螺丝状小球，专往细胞里钻。

root: 拉丁语 virus（毒液、黏液）→ 科学拉丁语 virus（病毒）→ 英语 virus；同根词有 virulent。

sensesIntro.en: A Latin word for poison ends up meaning the smallest cause of illness, then the illness, then a program, then a harmful idea.
sensesIntro.cn: 拉丁的「毒」先是变成最小的病因，再变成那场病、那个程序，最后变成一个有害念头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spiked particle landing on a cell.
core.cn: 核心意象：落在细胞上的带刺颗粒。

branches.en: The agent branch: a virus rather than bacteria.
branches.cn: 病原分支：是病毒而非细菌。

branches.en: The illness branch: off work for a week with a virus.
branches.cn: 疾病分支：因病毒感染病休一周。

branches.en: The computer branch: a laptop slowed by a virus.
branches.cn: 电脑分支：被病毒弄慢的笔记本。

branches.en: The metaphor branch: envy as a virus of the mind.
branches.cn: 比喻分支：嫉妒是精神的病毒。

branches.en: The old branch: a poison in the blood.
branches.cn: 旧义分支：血中的毒。

intro.en: Vir- carries the Latin poison; -us was the Latin ending, and -al, -ology, -ist build modern words.
intro.cn: vir- 携带拉丁的「毒」，-us 是拉丁词尾，-al、-ology、-ist 搭出现代词。

latinIntro.en: Latin virus is recorded for a poison or a slime; the adjective virulentus is also recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 virus 有毒液、黏液义都有记录，形容词 virulentus 同样有记录。

items.example: The root carries the idea of poison.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根携带「毒」的意思。

items.example: The noun is Latin, not a coinage.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是拉丁词，不是新造词。

items.example: The ending stayed in Latin form.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾保留了拉丁形式。

definition_zh: 能见度；可见性；可见程度；（公众）关注度
definition_en: the distance one can see clearly, or the state of being able to be seen
core_image: 从山脊望向远处，一层层山影越来越淡
scene: 清晨的山路上雾很重，前面的路牌要走近才看得清。Fog cut visibility to less than fifty metres on the motorway.
sceneCN: 这里 visibility 是「能见度」（第 1 个义项：能看清的距离）；句意为大雾使高速路上的能见度降到不足五十米。从山脊望出去、远山越来越淡的那幅画面，正是这个词的形象。

pos.zh: 能见度；可见性；可见程度；关注度

collocations.phrase: raise the visibility of an issue
collocations.zh: 提高某个议题的关注度

derivatives.zh: 去掉后缀 -ity 得到的形容词，义为「可见的；明显的」
加 -ly 构成，义为「明显地」
加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「不可见性」
同根名词，义为「视力；愿景」

senses.title: The distance one can see
senses.definition: the distance at which objects can be clearly seen, especially in weather reports
senses.definitionCN: 能清晰看见物体的距离，尤用于天气报告
senses.example: Fog cut visibility to less than fifty metres on the motorway.
senses.exampleCN: 大雾使高速路上的能见度降到不足五十米。
senses.why: Latin videre, to see, gives vis-, and -ity names a quality, so visibility is literally the quality of being able to be seen.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 videre（看见）给出 vis-，-ity 表示性质，所以 visibility 字面上就是「能被看见的程度」。

senses.title: The state of being seen
senses.definition: the fact or degree of something being able to be seen at all
senses.definitionCN: 某物能否被看见、被看见到什么程度
senses.example: The tall trees limited the visibility of the path from the house.
senses.exampleCN: 高树挡住了从屋里看到小路的视线。
senses.why: Strip the weather away and the word still measures how much a thing can be seen.
senses.whyCN: 去掉天气的成分，这个词仍在衡量一件事物能被看到多少。

senses.title: Public attention
senses.definition: the degree to which a person or a cause is noticed by the public
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或一项事业被公众注意的程度
senses.example: The campaign gave the small charity national visibility.
senses.exampleCN: 这场宣传活动让那家小慈善机构获得全国关注。
senses.why: A cause that can be seen is a cause people can support, so being seen turned into being noticed publicly.
senses.whyCN: 看得见的事业才能得到支持，于是「被看见」变成了「被公众注意」。

senses.title: Clearness of a design or a text
senses.definition: the quality of being easy to see and read, in print or on a screen
senses.definitionCN: 印刷或屏幕上易于看见和阅读的程度
senses.example: Contrast improves the visibility of small text on a screen.
senses.exampleCN: 提高对比度可以改善屏幕上小字的清晰度。
senses.why: Typesetters and designers need the same quality as weather forecasters: how well a thing comes to the eye.
senses.whyCN: 排版者与设计师需要的品质和气象预报员一样：东西进入眼睛的效果有多好。

senses.title: The character of being plainly evident
senses.definition: the quality of something being obvious or clear to everyone
senses.definitionCN: 某事物对所有人都明显、清楚的性质
senses.example: The visibility of the mistake made the meeting awkward.
senses.exampleCN: 这个错误太显眼，让会议很尴尬。
senses.why: If a thing cannot be hidden, it is visible in a strong sense, and the noun names that plainness.
senses.whyCN: 若一件事藏不住，它就在强意义上可见，名词便指这种显而易见。

intro.en: Visibility comes from Latin videre, to see, through the adjective visibilis, able to be seen.
intro.cn: visibility 来自拉丁语 videre（看见），经由形容词 visibilis（能被看见的）。

items.en: Videre meant to see, and the stem vis- carries that meaning into many English words.
items.cn: videre 意为看见，词干 vis- 把这个意思带进许多英语词。

items.en: Visibilis was formed to mean able to be seen.
items.cn: visibilis 构造成「能被看见的」。

items.en: The abstract noun visibilitas named the quality of being seen.
items.cn: 抽象名词 visibilitas 指能被看见这一性质。

items.en: English took visibility in the sixteenth century, mainly in learned writing.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪引入 visibility，主要用于学术写作。

items.en: Aviation and motoring turned it into a measured distance in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 二十世纪航空与汽车交通把它变成一个可测的距离。

note.en: The first group holds the see-root family, the second the words for sight and for being noticed.
note.cn: 第一组收「看」词根族，第二组收视觉与被注意相关词。

entries.definition: The adjective, meaning able to be seen.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可见的」。

entries.definition: The adverb, meaning in a way that can be seen.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「明显地」。

entries.definition: The state of not being able to be seen.
entries.definitionCN: 看不见的状态。

entries.definition: Sight itself, or a picture seen in the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 看的能力，或心中所见之景。

entries.definition: The ability to see, or something seen.
entries.definitionCN: 看的能力，或所见之物。

entries.definition: The quality of being clear, in air, sound or writing.
entries.definitionCN: 空气、声音或文字清晰的性质。

entries.definition: Public attention given to a person or a product.
entries.definitionCN: 给予人或产品的公众注意。

entries.definition: The state of being important and noticed.
entries.definitionCN: 重要而受注意的状态。

normalIntro.en: The see-root plus -ity: a quality of being seen, measured in metres by pilots and drivers.
normalIntro.cn: 「看」词根加 -ity：一种被看见的性质，又被飞行员与司机用米来量。

normal.en: Vis- means to see, from Latin videre.
normal.cn: vis- 意为看见，源自拉丁语 videre。

normal.en: -ity turns visible into a quality, as in ability and clarity.
normal.cn: -ity 把 visible 变成性质名词，如 ability、clarity。

normal.en: Visibility is uncountable: poor visibility, not a visibility.
normal.cn: visibility 不可数：说 poor visibility。

normal.en: In weather it is a distance; in public life it is attention.
normal.cn: 在天气里它是距离，在公共生活中它是关注。

normal.en: Invisibility is the opposite, formed with in-.
normal.cn: invisibility 是反面，用 in- 构成。

abstract.en: See ridges fading one behind the other into haze.
abstract.cn: 想象一道道山脊越远越淡，没入雾中。

abstract.en: Hear a radio voice giving the distance in metres.
abstract.cn: 听广播报出以米计的距离。

abstract.en: Picture a sign that everyone in the street can read at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一块全街人都能同时看清的牌子。

examples.en: Visibility was poor on the mountain road that morning.
examples.cn: 那天早上山路的能见度很差。

examples.en: The new logo increased the brand's visibility.
examples.cn: 新标志提高了品牌的曝光度。

examples.en: Thick glass reduced the visibility of the numbers.
examples.cn: 厚玻璃让数字变得看不清。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「为扎必了体」——雾太浓，为看清路得扎着脖子，能见度实在太低。

root: 拉丁语 videre（看见）→ visibilis（可见的）→ 中世纪拉丁语 visibilitas → 英语 visibility；同根词有 visible、vision、advise。

sensesIntro.en: How well a thing comes to the eye becomes a measured distance, then a share of public attention, then a plainness nobody can miss.
sensesIntro.cn: 「东西进入眼睛的效果」先变成可测的距离，再变成公众关注的一份，最后变成谁都躲不开的显而易见。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: ridges fading into haze.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道道山脊没入雾中。

branches.en: The weather branch: fifty metres on the motorway.
branches.cn: 天气分支：高速路上五十米。

branches.en: The sightline branch: trees blocking the path from the house.
branches.cn: 视线分支：树挡住从屋里看小路的视线。

branches.en: The attention branch: a small charity on national news.
branches.cn: 关注分支：小慈善机构上了全国新闻。

branches.en: The design branch: small text made readable by contrast.
branches.cn: 设计分支：靠对比度让小字可读。

branches.en: The plainness branch: a mistake everyone could see.
branches.cn: 明显分支：人人都看得见的错误。

intro.en: Vis- means to see, -ibilis and -ity make an adjective and then a quality, and in- negates it.
intro.cn: vis- 意为看见，-ibilis 与 -ity 依次造出形容词与性质名词，in- 表示否定。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre and visibilis are recorded, as is the medieval noun visibilitas.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre 与 visibilis 均有记录，中世纪名词 visibilitas 同样有记录。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根携带「看见」之义。

items.example: The verb also gives vision and video.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词还生出 vision 与 video。

definition_zh: 看得见的；可见的；明显的；显而易见的
definition_en: able to be seen, or easy to notice and recognise
core_image: 远处有个小点，越走越清楚，最后能认出是一个人
scene: 雾散了一点，山顶的塔终于从灰白里显出来。The far tower was not visible until the cloud lifted.
sceneCN: 这里 visible 是「看得见的」（第 1 个义项：能被眼睛看到）；句意为云散之前那座远处的塔看不见。由小点变成清晰人影的那段过程，就是这个词的形象。

pos.zh: 看得见的；可见的；明显的

derivatives.zh: 加 -ly 构成，义为「明显地」
加 -ity 构成，义为「能见度；可见性」
加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「看不见的」
同根名词，义为「视力；愿景」

senses.title: Able to be seen by the eye
senses.definition: able to be seen, because light reaches it and then the eye
senses.definitionCN: 因有光到达并被眼睛接收而能被看到
senses.example: The far tower was not visible until the cloud lifted.
senses.exampleCN: 云散之前，那座远处的塔是看不见的。
senses.why: Latin videre, to see, gives the stem vis-, and -ible means able to be; visible is literally able to be seen.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 videre（看见）给出词干 vis-，-ible 表示「能被…的」，visible 字面上就是「能被看见的」。

senses.title: Easy to notice
senses.definition: clear enough to be noticed at once, though not necessarily seen by the eye
senses.definitionCN: 清楚到能被立即注意到，尽管不一定用眼去看
senses.example: There were visible signs of strain in his face.
senses.exampleCN: 他脸上有明显的疲惫迹象。
senses.why: What the eye can notice without effort becomes a general word for anything easy to detect.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛不费力就能注意到的东西，成了任何易被察觉之物的通用说法。

senses.title: Of light, within the range the eye can see
senses.definition: of radiation, having a wavelength the human eye responds to
senses.definitionCN: 指辐射的波长在人的眼睛能反应的范围内
senses.example: Visible light lies between the infrared and the ultraviolet.
senses.exampleCN: 可见光位于红外与紫外之间。
senses.why: Physics used the word for the narrow band of light that is literally able to be seen.
senses.whyCN: 物理学用这个词指那一段字面上能被看见的光。

senses.title: Open to public view
senses.titleCN: 公开可见的；可被查到的
senses.definition: of records or activity, able to be checked or seen by others
senses.definitionCN: 指记录或活动可被他人查看
senses.example: The accounts are visible to every member of the club.
senses.exampleCN: 账目对俱乐部每位成员都可见。
senses.why: A thing to be checked must first be seen, so records are described as visible to those allowed to look.
senses.whyCN: 要被核对的东西先得能被看见，于是记录被描述为对被允许查看者可见。

senses.title: Prominent in public life
senses.definition: noticed often by the public, as a role or a person
senses.definitionCN: 被公众频繁注意，如某个角色或人物
senses.example: She became a visible figure in the campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 她成了这场运动中的显眼人物。
senses.why: The metaphor of being on view gives the modern sense of public prominence.
senses.whyCN: 「摆在人眼前」这个比喻给出了现代的公众显眼义。

intro.en: Visible is Latin visibilis, able to be seen, from videre, to see.
intro.cn: visible 即拉丁语 visibilis（能被看见的），来自 videre（看见）。

items.en: Videre meant to see, and its stem vis- spread into many later words.
items.cn: videre 意为看见，其词干 vis- 进入许多后来的词。

items.en: Visibilis added the ending -ibilis, meaning able to be, to the stem.
items.cn: visibilis 在词干上加 -ibilis（能被…的）。

items.en: Old French visible carried the word to English in the middle ages.
items.cn: 古法语 visible 在中世纪把这个词带进英语。

items.en: English used it first of things seen by the eye and soon of things merely plain.
items.cn: 英语先用它指眼睛所见之物，很快又指只是明白清楚的事。

items.en: Physics and administration then gave it the senses of visible light and visible records.
items.cn: 物理学与行政事务随后添上「可见光」与「可查阅记录」两义。

note.en: The first group holds the see-root family, the second the adjectives for clear and for hidden.
note.cn: 第一组收「看」词根族，第二组收表示清楚与隐藏的形容词。

entries.definition: The adverb, meaning in a way that can be seen.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「明显地」。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being visible.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可见性、能见度」。

entries.definition: The opposite adjective, unable to be seen.
entries.definitionCN: 反义形容词，义为「看不见的」。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning relating to seeing.
entries.definitionCN: 同根形容词，义为「视觉的」。

entries.definition: Seeming true, or plainly seen.
entries.definitionCN: 看来如此，或明显可见。

entries.definition: So clear that it cannot be missed.
entries.definitionCN: 清楚到不会漏掉。

entries.definition: Clear from the evidence at hand.
entries.definitionCN: 由现有证据看得很清楚。

entries.definition: Kept out of sight, the opposite of visible.
entries.definitionCN: 藏起来不被看见，与 visible 相对。

normalIntro.en: Vis- (see) plus -ible (able to be): a short pattern shared with audible and sensible.
normalIntro.cn: vis-（看见）加 -ible（能被…的）：与 audible、sensible 同一套构造。

normal.en: Visible is vis- plus -ible, able to be seen.
normal.cn: visible 是 vis- 加 -ible，义为「能被看见的」。

normal.en: In- makes invisible; -ly makes visibly; -ity makes visibility.
normal.cn: in- 构成 invisible，-ly 构成 visibly，-ity 构成 visibility。

normal.en: Visible light is only a small band of the spectrum.
normal.cn: 可见光只是光谱中很窄的一段。

normal.en: Apparent and evident are close, but visible is about being seen first.
normal.cn: apparent 与 evident 相近，visible 更强调先能被看见。

normal.en: A visible sign is one you notice without being told.
normal.cn: visible sign 是不用别人说就能注意到的迹象。

abstract.en: See a tiny mark on the horizon become a tower.
abstract.cn: 想象地平线上一个小点变成一座塔。

abstract.en: Hear a fact stated so plainly that nobody can miss it.
abstract.cn: 听一件事说得太直白，谁都不会漏掉。

abstract.en: Picture a record book open on a table for anyone to read.
abstract.cn: 想象一本记录簿摊在桌上，谁都能读。

examples.en: The coast was visible from the top of the hill.
examples.cn: 从山顶能看见海岸。

examples.en: There were no visible marks on the wall.
examples.cn: 墙上没有可见的痕迹。

examples.en: The stain is barely visible in this light.
examples.cn: 在这种光线下那块污迹几乎看不见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「为择伯」——为挑东西的伯父能一眼看见，因为东西摆在明处。

root: 拉丁语 videre（看见）→ visibilis（能被看见的）→ 古法语 visible → 英语 visible；同根词有 vision、visual、advise。

sensesIntro.en: To be seen by the eye spreads to being easy to notice, to light itself, to open records and to public prominence.
sensesIntro.cn: 「被眼睛看见」先扩到容易察觉、再到光本身、再到公开记录与公众显眼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a distant mark becoming a tower.
core.cn: 核心意象：远处的小点变成一座塔。

branches.en: The eye branch: the tower hidden by cloud.
branches.cn: 眼睛分支：被云遮住的塔。

branches.en: The notice branch: visible strain on a face.
branches.cn: 察觉分支：脸上明显的疲惫。

branches.en: The light branch: between infrared and ultraviolet.
branches.cn: 光分支：红外与紫外之间。

branches.en: The records branch: accounts open to members.
branches.cn: 记录分支：对会员公开的账目。

branches.en: The prominence branch: a visible figure in a campaign.
branches.cn: 显眼分支：运动中引人注目的人物。

intro.en: Vis- means to see; -ible, -ly, -ity and in- make the rest of the family.
intro.cn: vis- 意为看见，-ible、-ly、-ity、in- 造出其余词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre and visibilis are both recorded, so the root is secure.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre 与 visibilis 均有记录，词根可靠。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根携带「看见」之义。

items.example: It also gives video and evident.
items.exampleCN: 它还生出 video 与 evident。
它构成 visible 与 audible。

definition_zh: 视力；视觉；幻象；愿景；远见
definition_en: the ability to see, something seen in the mind or in a dream, or a plan for the future
core_image: 眼望窗外，却在心里看见一座还没建成的城
scene: 夜里他睡不着，眼前总是同一幅画面：老屋后面那片绿地上，孩子们在跑。The founder had a clear vision of what the school could become.
sceneCN: 这里 vision 是「愿景」（第 1 个义项之外的常用义：心中设想、指向未来的图景）；句意为创办人清楚地看见这所学校可以变成什么样子。望着窗外却在心里看见未来，就是这个词的形象。

pos.zh: 视力；视觉；幻象；愿景；远见

collocations.phrase: a clear vision of the future

derivatives.zh: 由 vis- 加 -ual 构成，义为「视觉的」
加 -ary 构成，义为「有远见者；空想家」
同根形容词，义为「可见的」
加前缀 en- 构成，义为「设想；展望」

senses.title: The power of sight
senses.definition: the ability of the eyes to see, or the sense by which things are seen
senses.definitionCN: 眼睛看见的能力，或借此感知事物的感官
senses.example: His vision is still sharp at eighty.
senses.exampleCN: 他八十岁时视力仍然敏锐。
senses.why: Latin videre meant to see, and the noun visio named the act of seeing; the word came into English naming the sense itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 videre 意为看见，名词 visio 指看这一行为；进入英语时它指的就是这种感官。

senses.title: Something seen in the mind or a dream
senses.definition: an image seen in a dream, a trance or the imagination
senses.definitionCN: 在梦境、恍惚或想象中看到的形象
senses.example: She had a vision of the house as it had been in her childhood.
senses.exampleCN: 她恍惚看见这栋房子还是童年的模样。
senses.why: A sight that is not there but is seen as if it were is the second step: the eye of the mind replaces the eye of the head.
senses.whyCN: 本不在那里却像真的看见，这是第二步：心眼取代了肉眼。

senses.title: A picture of what could be
senses.definition: an imagined future state that guides what one does now
senses.definitionCN: 指引当下行动的未来图景
senses.example: The founder had a clear vision of what the school could become.
senses.exampleCN: 创办人清楚地看见了这所学校可以变成什么样子。
senses.why: Of all the images the mind can see, the one of a future worth building became the modern main sense.
senses.whyCN: 心中能见的诸多影像里，「值得建起来的未来」成了现代的主要义项。

senses.title: An idea of how to act
senses.definition: a conception of how something should be done, often shared with others
senses.definitionCN: 对某事该如何做的看法，常与他人共享
senses.example: The two leaders had different visions of the city's future.
senses.exampleCN: 两位领袖对城市未来有不同的构想。
senses.why: A plan is a picture others can share, so the word for an inner image also names a common idea of what to do.
senses.whyCN: 计划是可以共享的图景，于是表示心中影像的词也指共同的行动设想。

senses.title: A religious appearance
senses.definition: an appearance of a holy figure or a message seen in a religious state
senses.definitionCN: 宗教情境中见到神圣形象或得到的信息
senses.example: The story tells of a vision at the well.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事讲的是井边的异象。
senses.why: A sight given in a religious state is the oldest branch of the word, and it keeps the plain sense of something seen.
senses.whyCN: 在宗教状态中得到的景象是这个词最古老的分支，仍保留「看见某物」的本义。

intro.en: Vision comes from Latin visio, a seeing, from the verb videre, to see.
intro.cn: vision 来自拉丁语 visio（看见），源自动词 videre（看见）。

items.en: Videre meant to see, and visio named the act or the result of seeing.
items.cn: videre 意为看见，visio 指看的行为或所见之结果。

items.en: The noun was used both for sight with the eyes and for images seen in sleep or revelation.
items.cn: 这个名词既指肉眼看，也指在睡梦或启示中见到的影像。

items.en: Old French vision carried both senses into English.
items.cn: 古法语 vision 把这两层意思一起带进英语。

items.en: Religious writing kept the supernatural sense widely alive for centuries.
items.cn: 宗教写作使超自然的异象义流传数百年。

items.en: Modern management and politics gave the word its forward-looking sense of a guiding plan.
items.cn: 现代管理与政治给了这个词指向未来的蓝图义。

note.en: The first group holds the see-root family, the second the words for sight, dream pictures and plans.
note.cn: 第一组收「看」词根族，第二组收视觉、幻想与计划类词。

entries.definition: The plural form of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词复数。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning relating to seeing or to pictures.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「视觉的、画面上的」。

entries.definition: A person with plans beyond the present, or such a plan.
entries.definitionCN: 有超前眼光的人，或这样的构想。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to picture something in the future.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「设想、展望」。

entries.definition: The everyday word for the power of seeing.
entries.definitionCN: 「看」的能力的日常说法。

entries.definition: Images during sleep, and informally, hopes.
entries.definitionCN: 睡梦中的影像，口语中也指愿望。

entries.definition: The general power of forming pictures in the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 在心中形成图像的一般能力。

entries.definition: The ability to see what is likely to happen.
entries.definitionCN: 预见事情可能如何发展的能力。

normalIntro.en: One see-root runs from eyesight to dream to a picture of the future.
normalIntro.cn: 一个「看」词根从眼力一路走到梦境，再走到未来的图景。

normal.en: Vision and visible share Latin videre, to see.
normal.cn: vision 与 visible 共享拉丁语 videre（看见）。

normal.en: Visionary means both a person of foresight and a mere dreamer.
normal.cn: visionary 既指有远见者，也指空想者。

normal.en: Blurred vision is about the eyes; a vision of the future is about the mind.
normal.cn: blurred vision 说眼睛，a vision of the future 说心思。

normal.en: The plural is visions; the adjective is visual.
normal.cn: 复数是 visions，形容词是 visual。

normal.en: Tunnel vision means seeing only one narrow thing.
normal.cn: tunnel vision 指只看见窄窄的一点。

abstract.en: See a lit window and a city that is not there yet.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇亮着的窗，和一座还没建成的城。

abstract.en: Hear someone describe a school before it exists.
abstract.cn: 听人描述一所尚未存在的学校。

abstract.en: Feel the difference between seeing badly and seeing far.
abstract.cn: 体会看不清与看得远之间的差别。

examples.en: His vision has faded since the operation.
examples.cn: 手术后他的视力变差了。

examples.en: The plan grew out of one woman's vision.
examples.cn: 这个方案源自一位女性的远见。

examples.en: She described a vision she had in a dream.
examples.cn: 她描述了梦中见到的一幅景象。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「为深」——为看得更深更远，才有这样的愿景。

root: 拉丁语 videre（看见）→ visio（看见、所见的影像）→ 古法语 vision → 英语 vision；同根词有 visible、visual、evident。

sensesIntro.en: The act of seeing splits into sight, into what appears though absent, and into a picture of the future worth building.
sensesIntro.cn: 看这一行为先分成眼力，再分成明明不在却出现在眼前的景象，最后变成值得建起的未来图景。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a window, and a city that is not there yet.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇窗，和一座尚未出现的城。

branches.en: The eyesight branch: sharp vision at eighty.
branches.cn: 视力分支：八十岁仍敏锐的目力。

branches.en: The apparition branch: the house as it once was.
branches.cn: 幻象分支：童年模样的房子。

branches.en: The future branch: what a school could become.
branches.cn: 未来分支：学校可以变成的样子。

branches.en: The plan branch: two leaders, two futures.
branches.cn: 构想分支：两位领袖，两种未来。

branches.en: The holy branch: a vision at the well.
branches.cn: 神圣分支：井边的异象。

intro.en: Vis- carries seeing; -ion makes the noun, and -ual, -ary, en- and -ity build the family.
intro.cn: vis- 携带「看见」之义，-ion 造出名词，-ual、-ary、en-、-ity 扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre and visio are both recorded, and visio is common in classical prose.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre 与 visio 均有记录，visio 在古典散文里很常见。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根携带「看见」之义。

items.example: It also gives evident and video.
items.exampleCN: 它还生出 evident 与 video。
